title: Keritot 3
description: Why the mishna counts thirty-six and no more: two prohibitions with one karet, whom the tally counts, Shabbat and idol worship counted once, and whether two karets or two death penalties under one prohibition divide the sin offering.
topics: 🫒 Two prohibitions, one karet: blending the anointing oil and applying it
🔢 Whom the tally counts: men or women, Rabbi Yishmael or Rabbi Akiva
✂️ Thirty-three sin offerings, and three karet cases to complete the list
🕯️ Shabbat and idol worship: unwitting of the day, intentional of the labors
📂 Rav Beivai: the mishna teaches the category of Shabbat, not each labor
⚖️ Rabbi Yirmeya’s dilemma: two karet or two death penalties under one prohibition
🦴 The necromancer and the sorcerer: what counts as an action
🦂 The ḥover ḥever, and Abaye on the hornet and the scorpion

a1.he: לַאֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁהִיא בַּת אָבִיו וּבַת אִמּוֹ, לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין עוֹנְשִׁין מִן הַדִּין.

a2.he: וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, סָבַר: עוֹנְשִׁין מִן הַדִּין. וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: יָלֵיף עוֹנֶשׁ מֵאַזְהָרָה.

a3.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא שְׁנֵי לָאוִין וְכָרֵת אֶחָד – חַלֵּק חַטָּאת בֵּינֵיהֶן. וּמַאי הִיא? מְפַטֵּם וְסָךְ, דִּכְתִיב: ״עַל בְּשַׂר אָדָם לֹא יִיסָךְ וּבְמַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ וְגוֹ׳״, כָּרֵת אֶחָד, דִּכְתִיב: ״אֲשֶׁר יִרְקַח כָּמֹהוּ וַאֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ עַל זָר וְנִכְרַת מֵעַמָּיו״.

a4.he: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלָאוִין מוּחְלָקִים, כָּרֵת דַּאֲחוֹתוֹ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי?

a5.he: לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק – כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ, לְרַבָּנַן מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לוֹמַר, שֶׁאֵין עוֹנְשִׁין מִן הַדִּין! לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְחַיֵּיב עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אָבִיו וְשֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ.

a6.he: וְרַבָּנַן? דְּנָפְקָא לְהוֹן מִן ״אֲחֹתוֹ״ דְרֵישָׁא. וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק? סָבַר ״אֲחוֹתוֹ״ דְרֵישָׁא אוֹרְחֵיהּ דִּקְרָא הִיא, וּמַפֵּיק לְחַלֵּק מֵ״אֲחֹתוֹ״ דְּסֵיפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא, לְחַלֵּק עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אָבִיו וְשֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ.

a7.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא: הַמְפַטֵּם אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן, הַמְפַטֵּם אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת, וְהַסָּךְ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה.

a8.he: לְמָה לִי דְּתַנְיָא הַמְפַטֵּם אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת בְּמִיצְעָא? לָאו הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: מָה קְטֹרֶת לָאו בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְחַיָּיבִים עָלֶיהָ כָּרֵת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ – אַף מְפַטֵּם שֶׁמֶן וְסָךְ נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ – חַיָּיבִים עָלָיו בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ?

a9.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִיתְנָא פִּיטּוּמִין בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי – נִיתְנִהוּ אֵיפוֹךְ: הַמְפַטֵּם אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת, וְהַמְפַטֵּם אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן, וְהַסָּךְ שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה, אַמַּאי פַּלְּגֵיהּ לְשֶׁמֶן? לָאו הָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּיֵשׁ חִילּוּק חַטָּאוֹת בֵּינֵיהֶן? שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a10.he: הַבָּא עַל הַזָּכוּר. תַּנָּא בְּמַאי קָא חָשֵׁיב?

a11.he: אִי בְּגַבְרֵי – דַּל הָאִשָּׁה הַנִּרְבַּעַת, וּבָצְרָא לַהּ חֲדָא! אִי בִּנְשֵׁי קָחָשֵׁיב – דַּל מִינְּהוֹן הַבָּא עַל הַזָּכוּר וְעַל הַבְּהֵמָה, וּבָצְרִי לְהוּ תַּרְתֵּי!

a12.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְעוֹלָם תַּנָּא גַּבְרֵי קָחָשֵׁיב, וְתָנֵי הָכִי: הַבָּא עַל הַזָּכוּר וְהֵבִיא זָכוּר עָלָיו, וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא, דְּאָמַר: חַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם.

a13.he: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי מְגַדֵּף בְּסֵיפֵיהּ, וּמוֹקְמִינַן לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא!

a14.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, וּבְרֵישָׁא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: הַבָּא עַל הַזָּכוּר וְהֵבִיא זָכוּר עָלָיו, לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ מִתַּרְתֵּי קְרָאֵי, מִ״וְּאֶת זָכָר לֹא תִשְׁכַּב״, וּמִ״וְּלֹא יִהְיֶה קָדֵשׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ – חַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם,

a15.he: לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת, דְּמֵחַד קְרָא נָפֵיק לֵיהּ: ״אֶת זָכָר לֹא תִשְׁכַּב״, קְרִי בֵּיהּ: לֹא תִשָּׁכֵיב!

a16.he: אֶלָּא: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וּבִמְגַדֵּף סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. אִי הָכִי, נִיתְנֵי נָמֵי: הַבָּא עַל הַבְּהֵמָה, וְהֵבִיא בְּהֵמָה עָלָיו!

a17.he: הָא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַבָּא עַל הַבְּהֵמָה וְהֵבִיא בְּהֵמָה עָלָיו, אַף לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת, דְּכִי כְּתִיב קְרָא – בְּגַבְרֵי כְּתִיב.

a18.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר: תַּנָּא תְּנִי שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ חַטָּאוֹת, וּתְנִי שָׁלֹשׁ כָּרֵיתוֹת, לְסַיּוֹמִינְהוּ בְּכָרֵיתוֹת.

a19.he: דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: פֶּסַח וּמִילָה בְּמִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה – פֶּסַח וּמִילָה אַמַּאי קָתָנֵי לְהוּ?

a20.he: וְאִיתֵּימָא לְאֵיתוֹיֵי קׇרְבָּן עֲלֵיהוֹן, מִי מַיְיתֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא: הוּקְּשָׁה כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעוֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה. וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה בְּיָד רָמָה״ –

a21.he: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה, אַף כֹּל שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה!

a22.he: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: תְּנָא שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מַאן דְּעָבְדִי בְּשׁוֹגֵג, וַהֲדַר תְּנָא שָׁלֹשׁ כָּרֵיתוֹת לְסַיּוֹמִינְהוּ לְכָרֵיתוֹת, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a23.he: הַמְחַלֵּל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת. אָמְרִי: שַׁבָּת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת הָוְויָין! אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: תַּנָּא שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת, דְּלָא מִחַיַּיב אֶלָּא חֲדָא.

a24.he: דְּתַנְיָא: ״הֵנָּה״ שֶׁהִיא ״אַחַת״ – שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת.

a25.he: וְנִיתְנֵי זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת, דְּמִחַיַּיב אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת!

a26.he: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְעָשָׂה מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה״ – פְּעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיב אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן, וּפְעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת. דְּתַנְיָא: ״אַחַת״ שֶׁהִיא ״הֵנָּה״ – זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת!

a27.he: תְּנָא שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ, דְּמֵחַטָּאת מִיהָא לָא מִיפְּטַר.

a28.he: וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, דְּקָתָנֵי: שִׁגְגַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּזְדוֹן עֲבוֹדוֹת.

a29.he: שִׁגְגַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּעָמַד בְּבֵית עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְסָבַר בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת הִיא וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה – הֲרֵי לִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם!

a30.he: וְאֶלָּא דַּחֲזָא אִנְדְּרָטָא וּסְגֵיד לֵהּ? אִי דְּקַבְּלֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ – בַּר סְקִילָה הוּא! וְאִי דְּלָא קַבְּלֵיהּ בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ – לָאו מִידֵּי הוּא!

a32.he: הָנִיחָא לְאַבַּיֵּי דְּאָמַר חַיָּיב, אֶלָּא לְרָבָא דְּאָמַר פָּטוּר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?

b1.he: אֶלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר מוּתָּר, דְּעַד כָּאן לָא קָבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן אֶלָּא אִי חֲדָא מִחַיַּיב אִי תַּרְתֵּי מִחַיַּיב, אָבֵל מִיפְּטַר לִגְמָרֵי לָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ.

b2.he: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּתִינוֹק שֶׁנִּשְׁבָּה לְבֵין הַגּוֹיִם, דְּיָדַע דַּאֲסִירָא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְהָנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לָא יָדַע דַּאֲסִירָן.

b3.he: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּגָדוֹל – כְּגוֹן דְּקָא טָעֵי בְּהָדֵין קְרָא: ״לֹא תַעֲשׂוּן אִתִּי אֱלֹהֵי כֶסֶף וֵאלֹהֵי זָהָב וְגוֹ׳״ סָבַר: כִּי אֲסִירָא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּכֶסֶף וְזָהָב, אֲבָל דְּמִינֵי אַחֲרִינֵי שַׁרְיָא, דְּהַיְינוּ שִׁגְגַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּזְדוֹן עֲבוֹדוֹת.

b4.he: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּיבִי אָמַר: תַּנָּא שֵׁם שַׁבָּת וְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה קָתָנֵי. מִמַּאי? מִדְּקָתָנֵי: הַבָּא עַל אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, וְהָא יֵשׁ בִּתּוֹ מֵאֲנוּסָתוֹ, דְּלָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ!

b5.he: אָמְרִי: דִּכְתִיבָן קָתָנֵי, דְּלָא כְּתִיבָן לָא קָתָנֵי.

b6.he: וְהָאִיכָּא בַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבַת בִּתָּהּ וּבַת בְּנָהּ, דִּכְתִיבָא, וְלָא קָתָנֵי! אֶלָּא: שֵׁם אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ קָתָנֵי? הָכִי נָמֵי: שֵׁם שַׁבָּת וְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה קָתָנֵי.

b7.he: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא רָמֵי דִּילֵיהּ אַדִּילֵיהּ: מִי אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי הָכִי, שֵׁם שַׁבָּת קָתָנֵי וְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה קָתָנֵי? וְהָאִיתְּמַר: הַמַּעֲלֶה אֵבְרֵי פְּנִים בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב, אֵבְרֵי חוּץ בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב.

b8.he: וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: ״אִי הָכִי, הָא דִּתְנַן: שְׁלֹשִׁים וָשֵׁשׁ כָּרֵיתוֹת בְּתוֹרָה – תְּלָתִין וּשְׁבַע נִינְהוּ, דְּאִיכָּא הַמַּעֲלֶה וְהַמַּעֲלֶה!״ מַאי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ? נִישְׁנֵי: שֵׁם הַעֲלָאָה קָתָנֵי!

b9.he: מִי דָּמֵי? שַׁבָּת וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה תְּנָא יָתְהוֹן אַבִּינְכֵיהוֹן, גַּבַּי כָּרֵיתוֹת, דְּאִירְיָא, מְשַׁנֵּי: ״שֵׁם שַׁבָּת קָתָנֵי שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה קָתָנֵי״, גַּבֵּי הַעֲלָאָה, מִי תְּנָא יָתְהוֹן בִּינְכֵיהוֹן דְּשַׁנִּי הָכִי?

b10.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא: שְׁתֵּי כָּרֵיתוֹת וְלָאו אֶחָד, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שׁוֹחֵט וְהֶעֱלָה קָאָמְרַתְּ? הָנֵי שְׁנֵי לָאוִין נִינְהוּ,

b11.he: אִי לְמַאן דְּגָמַר מִגְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה – נֶאֱמַר כָּאן הֲבָאָה וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן הֲבָאָה,

b12.he: מָה לְהַלָּן לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר – אַף כָּאן לֹא עָנַשׁ, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר.

b13.he: לְמַאן דְּמַיְיתֵי לַהּ בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ – אָמַר קְרָא: ״שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה... וְשָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה״, מַקִּישׁ שְׁחִיטָה לְהַעֲלָאָה, מָה הַעֲלָאָה לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר, אַף שְׁחִיטָה לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר.

b14.he: דִּלְמָא שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת וְלָאו אֶחָד קָאָמְרַתְּ? מָה הִיא – אוֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִי.

b15.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ דְּהָא פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ. דְּתָנוּ גַּבֵּי סַנְהֶדְרִין: בַּעַל אוֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִי, וְקַשְׁיָא לַן, וּמַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי סְקִילוֹת תָּנֵי יִדְּעוֹנִי, וְגַבֵּי כָּרֵיתוֹת לָא תָּנֵי יִדְּעוֹנִי?

b16.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הוֹאִיל וּשְׁנֵיהֶם בְּלָאו אֶחָד נֶאֶמְרוּ. וְנֵימָא יִדְּעוֹנִי, וְלָא נֵימָא בַּעַל אוֹב! קָסָבַר: הוֹאִיל וּפָתַח הַכָּתוּב בְּבַעַל אוֹב.

b17.he: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה. וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?

b18.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּהָא חֲלוּקִין הֵן בְּמִיתוֹת. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לְךָ: חֲלוּקָּה דְלָאו – הָוֵי חֲלוּקָּה, חֲלוּקָּה דְמִיתָה – לָא הָוְיָא חֲלוּקָּה.

b19.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ? קָסָבַר: מַאן תַּנָּא כָּרֵיתוֹת – רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, דְּאָמַר לָא בָּעִינַן מַעֲשֶׂה.

b20.he: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ? נְהִי דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא בָּעֵי מַעֲשֵׂה רַבָּה, מַעֲשֵׂה זוּטָא בָּעֵי.

b21.he: בַּעַל אוֹב, מַאי מַעֲשֶׂה אִית בֵּיהּ? הֲקָשַׁת זְרוֹעוֹתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה. מְגַדֵּף, מַאי מַעֲשֶׂה אִית בֵּיהּ? עֲקִימַת שְׂפָתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה.

b22.he: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין: הֲקָשַׁת זְרוֹעוֹתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה זוּטָא אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן. מֵיתִיבִי: בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה, כְּגוֹן שֶׁזִּיבַּח, וְקִיטֵּר, וְנִיסֵּךְ, וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה. וְקַשְׁיָא לַן, הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה לֵית בַּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה!

b23.he: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, דְּאָמַר לָא בָּעִינַן מַעֲשֶׂה. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, כְּפִיפַת קוֹמָתוֹ הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה. מִכְּלָל דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַלִּיבָּא דְרַבָּנַן כְּפִיפַת קוֹמָתוֹ לְרַבָּנַן לָא הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה. הֲקָשַׁת זְרוֹעוֹתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה?!

b24.he: וְאֶלָּא כִּי קָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הֲקָשַׁת זְרוֹעוֹתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה זוּטָא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֲבָל לְרַבָּנַן לָא הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה.

b25.he: אִי הָכִי, אַמַּאי תָּנֵי: יָצָא מְגַדֵּף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה? נִיתְנֵי: יָצָא מְגַדֵּף וּבַעַל אוֹב! חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי קָתָנֵי.

b26.he: וְלִיתְנֵי בַּעַל אוֹב וְלָא לִיתְנֵי מְגַדֵּף! מְגַדֵּף אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב כָּרֵת דִּילֵיהּ בִּמְקוֹם קׇרְבָּן, אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא.

b27.he: עוּלָּא אָמַר: בַּעַל אוֹב דְּקָתָנֵי בִּמְקַטֵּר לַשֵּׁד. מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, הַיְינוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה! אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: מְקַטֵּר לַשֵּׁד עַל מְנָת לְחַבְּרוֹ.

b28.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִם כֵּן, הָיִינוּ חוֹבֵר חָבֶר! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה חוֹבֵר חָבֶר כְּגוֹן זֶה, בִּסְקִילָה. וְאֶלָּא חוֹבֵר חֶבֶר דִּבְלָאו – הֵדֵין הוּא?

b29.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּדְתַנְיָא: ״וְחוֹבֵר חָבֶר״ – אֶחָד חוֹבֵר גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד חוֹבֵר קָטָן, וַאֲפִילּוּ חוֹבֵר לִנְחָשִׁים וְעַקְרַבִּים – חַיָּיב. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמִיצְמַד זִיבּוּרָא וְעַקְרַבָּא – אָסוּר, וְאִי קָאָתוּ בָּתְרֵיהּ – שְׁרֵי.

b30.he: לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר כְּפִיפַת קוֹמָתוֹ הָוֵי מַעֲשֵׂה, עֲקִימַת

messages.text: 3a
Continued from 2b: the Gemara asked what the Rabbis do with “his sister” in the latter clause of Leviticus 20:17, the verse that states karet for one’s sister. They require it…

to teach the halakha in the case of his sister who is both his father’s daughter and his mother’s daughter, and this serves to say that one does not administer punishment based on an a fortiori inference. Although the verses state a punishment both for one who engages in intercourse with his half sister who is his father’s daughter and for his half sister who is his mother’s daughter, one cannot learn via an a fortiori inference that he should also be punished for engaging in intercourse with his sister from both parents, as punishments are applied only when the Torah expressly imposes them.

notes.he: דלא אמרינן מה אחותו מן האב גרידא או מן האם גרידתא ענש עליה מן האב ומן האם לא כ"ש:
notes.en: That one does not administer punishment on the basis of an a fortiori inference: for we do not say: Just as [the Torah] punished for his sister from the father alone, or from the mother alone, [for his sister] from the father and from the mother, all the more so.

notes.he: תימה דלעיל משמע דאיצטריך אחותו לחלק על אחותו שהיא אחות אביו כו' הא חדא מיהא מחייב ואמאי הא אין עונשין מן הדין מיהו איכא למימר דמהא יליף כיון דגלי הכא ה"ה לעיל אך קשה דלקמן פ"ג (דף יג:) תנן יש אוכל אכילה אחת וחייב כו' ואמאי דלמא לא מחייב כיון דחמיר טפי וכ"ת דיליף מהכא מה לאחותו שכן לא הותרה מכללה ויש מתרצין דשאני הכא דליכא אלא איסור אחותו וחמירא טפי ב' צדדין מצד א' להכי אמרי' אין עונשין מן הדין אבל לקמן פ"ג דאיכא איסורין אחרים חייל שפיר ע"י כולל ומוסיף בבת אחת תימה מ"ש גבי בתו מאנוסתו דיליף ק"ו (בסנהדרין עז.) מבת בתו דחשיב גלוי מילתא ולא הוי אזהרה מן הדין וי"ל משום דבת בתו באה מכח קורבת בתו וא"א לבת בתו בלא בתו אבל הכא משכחת אחותו בת אביו שלא בת אמו או להפך:
notes.en:
In brief: To say that one does not administer punishment on the basis of an a fortiori inference: This is puzzling, since above “his sister” was needed to divide the offerings for a sister who is also his father’s sister, so he is liable at least one; why, if one does not punish by inference? Answer: he learns it from here, since the verse revealed it here.
But below, in chapter 3 (13b), the mishna rules “There is one who eats a single eating and is liable” to several offerings; why, if perhaps the graver case is not liable? And one cannot learn it from here, for a sister is unique in that she was never permitted out of her general prohibition. Some answer: here there is only the prohibition of his sister, a sister on two sides being graver than on one, so one does not punish by inference; there, other prohibitions take effect through the rules of an inclusive prohibition, an added prohibition and prohibitions taking effect at once.
It is puzzling: why, for his daughter from the woman he raped, does the Gemara (Sanhedrin 77a) derive it a fortiori from his daughter’s daughter, treating it as merely revealing the matter and not as a warning derived by inference? Answer: a daughter’s daughter comes through the relationship of his daughter and cannot exist without her, whereas a sister can be his father’s daughter and not his mother’s, or the reverse. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: And Rabbi Yitzḥak, who does not interpret the verses in this manner, maintains that one administers punishment based on an a fortiori inference.

And if you wish, say instead a different reason why Rabbi Yitzḥak does not require this exposition: He derives the punishment of karet for engaging in intercourse with a sister from both parents from the warning, i.e., the prohibition that is stated with regard to her. Just as the verse explicitly prohibited engaging in intercourse with a sister from both parents, so too, the same punishment of karet applies to engaging in intercourse with her as it does to engaging in intercourse with other forbidden relatives.

notes.he: לר"י אין עונשין מן הדין ועונש באחותו מן האב ומן האם לר' יצחק נפקא ליה דיליף עונש מאזהרה כשם שהזהיר עליה כשאר עריות כך ענש עליה ואזהרה דידה מפרש במסכת מכות (דף יד.) דאמר קרא ערות בת אביך או בת אמך אין לי אלא בת אביך שלא בת אמך ובת אמך שלא בת אביך בת אביך ואמך מנין ת"ל אחותך היא לא תגלה ערותה וכשם שהזהיר עליה כך ענש עליה:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: [even if,] according to Rabbi Yitzḥak, one does not administer punishment on the basis of an inference, Rabbi Yitzḥak derives the punishment for his sister from his father and from his mother in that he learns punishment from the warning: just as [the Torah] warned about her as about the other forbidden relatives, so it punished for her. Her warning is explained in tractate Makkot (14a): the verse states, “The nakedness of your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter”; I have only your father’s daughter who is not your mother’s daughter, and your mother’s daughter who is not your father’s daughter. From where [do I know] your father’s daughter who is also your mother’s daughter? The verse states: “She is your sister; you shall not uncover her nakedness.” And just as it warned about her, so it punished for her.

messages.text: Anywhere you find two different prohibitions, and only one punishment of karet is stated for both of them, you should divide the sin offering between them, i.e., if one transgressed both prohibitions unwittingly he is liable to bring a sin offering for each.

notes.he: שאם עשאן שניהם בהעלם אחת חייב שתים:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar said: divide the sin offerings: so that if he did both of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable to two.

messages.text: And what is this case? One who blends the anointing oil according to the specifications of the oil prepared by Moses in the wilderness, for purposes other than use in the Temple, and one who applies this anointing oil to the skin of a person, as it is written: “Upon the flesh of man it shall not be applied, neither shall you make any like it according to its composition” (Exodus 30:32).

verse.he: עַל־בְּשַׂר אָדָם לֹא יִיסָךְ וּבְמַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ כָּמֹהוּ קֹדֶשׁ הוּא קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה לָכֶם׃
verse.en: It must not be rubbed on any person’s body, and you must not make anything like it in the same proportions; it is sacred, to be held sacred by you.

messages.text: These are two prohibitions, one for applying the oil and the other for blending it, and one karet is stated with regard to both, as it is written: “Whoever compounds any like it, or whoever puts any of it upon a stranger, he shall be cut off from his people” (Exodus 30:33).

verse.he: אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִרְקַח כָּמֹהוּ וַאֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ עַל־זָר וְנִכְרַת מֵעַמָּיו׃ {ס}
verse.en: Anyone who compounds its like, or puts any of it on a lay person, shall be cut off from kin.

messages.text: But accordingly, once there are separate prohibitions stated in the Torah with regard to engaging in intercourse with all forbidden relatives (Leviticus, chapter 18), and at the conclusion of that passage it is written: “For whoever shall do any of these abominations, the souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people” (Leviticus 18:29), it is indicated that the punishments of karet or a sin offering apply to all these prohibitions.
messages.quote: two different prohibitions, and only one punishment of karet

verse.he: כִּי כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְנִכְרְתוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָעֹשֹׂת מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּם׃
verse.en: All who do any of those abhorrent things—such persons shall be cut off from among their people.

messages.text: If so, why do I need the punishment of karet that the Merciful One writes with regard to one’s sister, in a separate passage: “And they shall be cut off in the sight of the children of their people; he has uncovered his sister’s nakedness” (Leviticus 20:17)?

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִקַּח אֶת־אֲחֹתוֹ בַּת־אָבִיו אוֹ בַת־אִמּוֹ וְרָאָה אֶת־עֶרְוָתָהּ וְהִיא־תִרְאֶה אֶת־עֶרְוָתוֹ חֶסֶד הוּא וְנִכְרְתוּ לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי עַמָּם עֶרְוַת אֲחֹתוֹ גִּלָּה עֲוֺנוֹ יִשָּׂא׃
verse.en: If a man marries his sister, the daughter of either his father or his mother, so that he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace; they shall be excommunicated in the sight of their kinsfolk. He has uncovered the nakedness of his sister, he shall bear the guilt.

notes.he: דפרט בה קרא למאי אתא:
notes.en: Karet with regard to his sister: which the verse spelled out for her separately; what does it come for?

notes.he: הגה"ה כיון דלאוין מחלקין לא מיבעי ליה לחלק על אחותו שהיא אחות אביו ואחות אמו שהרי יש בה ג' לאוין:
notes.en: A gloss: Since the prohibitions [themselves] divide, [the verse] is not needed to divide for his sister who is his father’s sister and his mother’s sister, for she has three prohibitions.

notes.he: ה"ג לר' יצחק כדאית ליה לרבנן מיבעי להו לאחותו בת אביו ואמו לומר שאין עונשין מן הדין - וכוליה קרא משום אחותו דסיפא אתא ובשביל חדוש אחד דרך לשנות פרשה שנאמרה:
notes.en: This is the reading: “According to Rabbi Yitzḥak, per his opinion; the Rabbis require it for his sister who is his father’s daughter and his mother’s daughter, to say that one does not administer punishment on the basis of an inference.” And the whole verse comes because of “his sister” in the latter clause; for the sake of a single new point it is the way [of the Torah] to repeat a passage that was already stated.

notes.he: לרבי יצחק מיבעי ליה כו' עד סיפא ל"ג לה ופירוש משובש הוא מתלמידים טועין עד כאן הגה"ה:
notes.en: “According to Rabbi Yitzḥak he requires it,” etc., up to “the latter clause”: we do not have this in our text; it is a corrupt explanation from mistaken students. End of the gloss. [The passage meant appears to be the one in our printed Gemara that runs from “According to Rabbi Yitzḥak, he derives” to “in the latter clause,” shown in the next few messages.]

notes.he: אע"ג דחטאת לא אתי אלא במקום כרת אפי' [הכי] כיון דכתיבי ב' לאוין וכרת אחת משמע כרת אכל לאו לאו. וכי מאחר דלאוין מחלקין לחטאות הוא הדין לעריות דאית בהו הרבה לאוין וכרת אחת. אלא כרת באחותו אמאי איצטריך וקסבר ר' יצחק אחותו דרישיה דקרא לאו לדרשא אתי אלא אורחיה דקרא הוא ולגופיה איצטריך איש אשר יקח את אחותו ואחות דסיפיה מיבעי ליה לחלק. ואי קשיא אמאי קאמר ר' יצחק אחותו דרישא אורחיה דקרא הוא הא מפיק ליה לדונו בכרת ולא במלקות. ההוא לא מפיק אלא מכרת ולא מאחותו. ואמרי לן ר' דמס' מכות קא מהדר האי אי בעית תימא יליף עונש מאזהרה עלה דר' יצחק דאמר עונשין מן הדין וקאמר אי בעית תימא אחותו בת אביו ובת אמו יליף עונש מאזהרה ולא מן הדין שהרי כתיב אזהרה באחותו בת אביו ובת אמו דכתיב ערות בת אשת אביך מולדת אביך ויליף עונש מאזהרה. והכא לא מיתוקמא הכי משום דרבנן לא בעי ילפי הכי עונשין מאזהרה אלא מיתבעי להו כרת באחותו לומר שאין עונשין מן הדין:
notes.en: Divide the sin offerings between them: even though a sin offering comes only where there is karet, even so, since two prohibitions are written and one karet, it implies karet for each prohibition. And since prohibitions divide the sin offerings, the same applies to forbidden relations, which have many prohibitions and one karet. So why was karet with regard to his sister needed? And Rabbi Yitzḥak holds that “his sister” at the start of the verse is not for exposition but is the manner of the verse, needed for itself: “a man who takes his sister”; and “sister” at its end he needs to divide. And if you ask: why does Rabbi Yitzḥak say “his sister” in the first clause is the manner of the verse, when he derives from it that the sinner is judged with karet and not with lashes? He derives that only from “karet,” not from “his sister.” And our teacher told us that it is the Gemara in tractate Makkot that brings this “if you wish, say: he derives the punishment from the warning” with regard to Rabbi Yitzḥak, who says one administers punishment on the basis of an inference. It says: if you wish, say: for his sister who is his father’s daughter and his mother’s daughter, he derives the punishment from the warning and not from an inference, for a warning is written for her, as it is written: “The nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, born to your father” [Leviticus 18:11], and he derives the punishment from the warning. Here it cannot be explained so, because the Rabbis do not derive punishments from warnings in this way; rather, they need karet with regard to his sister to say that one does not administer punishment on the basis of an inference.

messages.text: This verse is required to teach one halakha according to the opinion of the Rabbis, and one halakha according to Rabbi Yitzḥak, per his opinion.
According to the opinion of the Rabbis, they require this verse to say that one does not administer punishment based on an a fortiori inference.

According to Rabbi Yitzḥak, he derives that this verse comes to deem one liable to bring three separate sin offerings for unwittingly engaging in intercourse with his own sister who is also his father’s sister and who is also his mother’s sister.
And as for the Rabbis, from where do they derive this halakha?
One can say that they derive it from the term “his sister” written in the first clause of the verse: “And if a man shall take his sister” (Leviticus 20:17).

And Rabbi Yitzḥak holds that one cannot derive a halakha from the term “his sister” written in the first clause, as it is the manner of the verse to describe the case in detail before stating the prohibition that applies to it. And therefore he derives from the term “his sister” written in the latter clause of the verse that this comes to separate between the prohibitions and render one liable to bring three separate sin offerings for engaging in intercourse with his own sister who is also his father’s sister and who is also his mother’s sister.
We learn in the mishna as well: And one who blends the anointing oil, and one who blends the incense, and one who applies the anointing oil to his skin.
messages.quote: One who blends the anointing oil, and one who applies this anointing oil

notes.he: כר' אלעזר אמר ר' אושעיא דלאוין מחלקין:
notes.en: We too learned it: in accordance with Rabbi Elazar’s statement in the name of Rabbi Oshaya that prohibitions divide [the sin offerings].

messages.text: Why do I need the tanna to teach the clause: One who blends the incense, in the middle, between the two cases concerning the anointing oil? Is it not correct that this is what the mishna teaches us: Just as blending the incense is an independent prohibition and one is liable to receive karet for it by itself, and to bring a sin offering for its unwitting transgression, so too, with regard to one who blends the anointing oil and one who applies the anointing oil to his skin, since they are each an independent prohibition, one is liable to receive karet for each action by itself, and to bring a sin offering for the unwitting transgression of each of them.

notes.he: על כל אחד כי עביד להו בהעלם אחת:
notes.en: And one is liable for it by itself: for each one, when he does them in one lapse of awareness.

notes.he: דמה קטרת לאו בפ"ע דכתיב והקטרת אשר תעשה במתכונתה לא תעשו וחייב עליה בפ"ע כדכתיב איש אשר יעשה כמוה להריח בה ונכרת:
notes.en: For just as the incense is an independent prohibition, as it is written: “And the incense that you shall make, according to its composition you shall not make” [Exodus 30:37], and one is liable for it by itself, as it is written: “Whoever shall make like it, to smell it, shall be cut off” [Exodus 30:38].

messages.text: And if you would say the mishna uses this order because it wants to teach the two cases involving blending together, let the tanna teach those two halakhot in the reverse order: One who blends the incense, and one who blends the anointing oil, and one who applies the anointing oil. In this manner the two clauses addressing blending would be adjacent, and likewise the two clauses addressing the anointing oil would be adjacent.

notes.he: וכי תימא מיהא לא איריא דמשום הכי תנא מפטם את הקטרת במיצעי משום דקא בעי למיתנייא פיטומין גבי הדדי א"כ נתנהו איפוך:
notes.en: And if you say there is no proof from this, for he taught “one who blends the incense” in the middle because he wants to teach the two blendings next to each other: if so, let him teach them in the reverse order.

messages.text: Why did the tanna divide the cases involving the anointing oil by teaching the halakha of one who blends the incense in between them? Is it not correct that this teaches us that there is a separation between the two prohibitions, requiring one to bring two sin offerings?
Conclude from the mishna that this is the case.

§ The mishna included in its list of those liable to receive karet a male who engages in intercourse with another male or one who copulates with an animal, and a woman who brings an animal upon her to engage in bestiality. According to what criteria does the tanna of the mishna tally the prohibitions in the mishna?

Rabbi Yoḥanan explained that the tally stated in the mishna serves to teach that one who violated every prohibition against engaging in forbidden intercourse in a single lapse of awareness is liable to receive punishment for each and every one. Which individual could have committed all these transgressions?

notes.he: מכדי אמרן לעיל מניינא להכי אתא שאם עשאן כולן כו' היכי משכחת לה לשלשים וארבע חטאות בחד:
notes.en: The tanna, what is he counting? Now, we said above that the count comes for this: that if he did all of them [in one lapse of awareness he is liable for each one]. How can you find thirty-four sin offerings in one [person]?

messages.text: If he is referring to prohibitions transgressed by men, then one should remove the case of a woman who brings an animal upon her to engage in bestiality, and if so, one case of karet is lacking from the tally.

notes.he: הוא דרבע לבהמה:
notes.en: A man: it is he who copulates with an animal.

notes.he: קא חשיב דהני ל"ו כריתות אי עבדי להו ל"ו גברי מיחייבי כל חד כרת א"כ דל אשה הנרבעת לבהמה מבינייהו:
notes.en: If he is counting men: that if thirty-six men committed these thirty-six cases of karet, each would be liable to karet; if so, remove the woman who is the object of bestiality from among them.

messages.text: If he is referring to prohibitions transgressed by women, one should remove from them the case of a male who engages in intercourse with another male or with an animal, and if so, two cases of karet are lacking from the tally.

notes.he: כגון שנבעלה לבנה ולבן בעלה ולחמיה ולחתנה ולבהמה וכן כולם:
notes.en: A woman: for example, where she had intercourse with her son, and with her husband’s son, and with her father-in-law, and with her son-in-law, and with an animal; and likewise all of them.

notes.he: דאין כאן צד אשה. פסח ומילה לא מצי למיפרך דלאו משום חטאות נקט להו דהא לאו בני קרבן נינהו דאין קרבן אלא על לאו כדמפרש לקמן:
notes.en: One who has intercourse with a male and with an animal: for there is no woman’s side to these. As for the Paschal offering and circumcision, he cannot raise an objection from them, for [the tanna] did not list them on account of sin offerings, since they are not subject to an offering at all: an offering comes only for a prohibition, as is explained below.

notes.he: דאי עבדי להו ל"ו נשי גבי [הדדי] מיחייבא כל חדא כרת:
notes.en: If he is counting women: that if thirty-six women committed them, each would be liable to karet.

notes.dh: דל מיניהון הבא על הזכור ועל הבהמה
notes.he: דהני לא מיתוקמי אלא בגברי ובצר להו תרתי אי אמרת מילה נמי הא ליתא בנשי:
notes.en: Remove from them one who has intercourse with a male and with an animal: for these can be explained only with men, and two are lacking from them. And if you mention circumcision too, that does not apply to women [either].

messages.text: Actually, the tanna is referring to prohibitions transgressed by men. One should remove the case of a woman who brings an animal upon her to engage in bestiality, and instead teach the mishna like this: A male who engages in intercourse with another male, and a male who brings another male upon him to engage in intercourse.

notes.dh: הא לא קשיא דלא מיירי אלא בלאוין
notes.he: ותני הכי דל אשה הנרבעת ותני הכי במקומה והביא זכור עליו דהוא נשכב לזכר:
notes.en: This is not difficult, for it speaks only of prohibitions. [A note in the printed text: it appears it should read: Actually he counts men, and as for your objection “remove the woman who is the object of bestiality,” teach thus in its place, etc.] And teach thus: remove the woman who is the object of bestiality, and teach in its place: “and brought a male upon himself,” which is one who is lain with by a male.

messages.text: And this mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, who says that one who transgresses both of these prohibitions in a single lapse of awareness is liable to bring two sin offerings.

notes.he: בפרק ד' מיתות:
notes.en: And it is Rabbi Yishmael: [as stated] in the chapter Arba Mitot [of Sanhedrin].

messages.text: But from the fact that the mishna teaches in its latter clause the case of one who blasphemes, and we interpret this clause in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, it may be inferred that the first clause of the mishna is also in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.
messages.quote: in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael

notes.he: בכלל כריתות מגדף לאשמועינן דמביא קרבן ומוקמי לה לקמן כר״ע דאמר בסוף פירקין (כריתות דף ז.) מגדף מביא קרבן רישא נמי ר״ע:
notes.en: But from the fact that it teaches the blasphemer among those liable to karet, to teach us that he brings an offering, and we establish it below in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who said at the end of our chapter (Keritot 7a) that a blasphemer brings an offering, the first clause too is Rabbi Akiva.

notes.dh: ור' ישמעאל הוא דאמר חייב שתים דנפיק ליה מתרי קראי כדאמר לקמן
notes.he: והא מדקתני מגדף בהני ומוקמי' לה כר' עקיבא דלא בעי מעשה אלא רישא נמי ר' עקיבא היא ור' עקיבא סבירא ליה בהבא על הזכור והביא זכור עליו דאינו חייב אלא אחת א"כ בצרא להו חדא:
notes.en: And it is Rabbi Yishmael, who says he is liable to two, since he derives it from two verses, as is said below. But from the fact that it teaches the blasphemer among these, and we explain it in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who does not require an action, the first clause too is Rabbi Akiva; and Rabbi Akiva holds that one who has intercourse with a male and brought a male upon himself is liable only one. If so, one is lacking from them.

messages.text: And if you would say the entire mishna is in fact in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, and with regard to the halakha listed in the first clause he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, that is not tenable,

notes.he: וכי תימא כולה מתניתין ר' עקיבא וברישא בהבא על הזכור סבר לה ר' עקיבא כר' ישמעאל דחייב שתים. ומן לא יהיה קדש היינו שלא יהא נשכב כזונה:
notes.en: And if you say the whole mishna is Rabbi Akiva, and in the first clause, about one who has intercourse with a male, Rabbi Akiva holds like Rabbi Yishmael that he is liable to two. And “There shall not be a sodomite” means that he should not be lain with like a prostitute.

messages.text: In the case of a male who engages in intercourse with another male, and a male who brings another male upon him to engage in intercourse, according to the statement of Rabbi Yishmael, who derives these prohibitions from two separate verses, from: “And you shall not lie with a man as with a woman” (Leviticus 18:22),

verse.he: וְאֶת־זָכָר לֹא תִשְׁכַּב מִשְׁכְּבֵי אִשָּׁה תּוֹעֵבָה הִוא׃
verse.en: Do not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abhorrence.

notes.he: בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין נד:) לא יהיה קדש אזהרה לנשכב ועונש מגזירה שוה דכתיב וגם קדש היה בארץ. ואי קשיא גבי עריות היכן מצינו אזהרה לאשה כמו לזכר דאשכחן בכולהו לאו פריק הכי שאני התם כיון דאיהי נמי מיתהנייא משכיבה קרינא בה הנפשות העושות אבל משכב זכר דלא מתהני בעי אזהרה. ובגברי כתיב דאין זכור לבהמה ולא מיקרי קדישות:
notes.en: As Rabbi Abbahu said: in the chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 54b). “There shall not be a sodomite” is the warning for the one who is lain with, and the punishment comes from a verbal analogy, as it is written: “And there were also sodomites in the land” [I Kings 14:24]. And if you ask: with the other forbidden relations, where do we find a warning for the woman as for the man, since with all of them we find the prohibition [addressed to the man]? One answers thus: there it is different, since she too derives pleasure from the lying, “the souls that do them” [Leviticus 18:29] applies to her. But in male intercourse, where [the one lain with] does not derive pleasure, a warning is needed. And [the verse] is written with regard to men, for there is no “male” with an animal, and it is not called sodomy.

messages.text: and from: “There shall not be a sodomite of the sons of Israel” (Deuteronomy 23:18), which is referring to one who engages in homosexual intercourse passively, one who transgresses both of these prohibitions in a single lapse of awareness is liable to bring two sin offerings.

verse.he: לֹא־תִהְיֶה קְדֵשָׁה מִבְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא־יִהְיֶה קָדֵשׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en: No Israelite woman shall be a consecrated worker, uncertain. In contrast to others “cult prostitute.” nor shall any Israelite man be a consecrated worker. uncertain. See previous note.

notes.he: תימה מתני' היכי מתוקמא דהא אלא יהיה קדש לא כתיב כרת והיכי משכחת בה חיוב חטאת וי"ל דכיון דכתיב כרת אמשכב זכור הוי ליה ב' לאוין וכרת אחד:
notes.en: According to Rabbi Yishmael, who derives it, etc.: This is puzzling: how is the mishna to be explained? Karet is not written with “There shall not be a sodomite”; so how can there be liability for a sin offering for it? One can say: since karet is written for male intercourse, it is two prohibitions and one karet.

messages.text: By contrast, according to the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, he is liable to bring only one sin offering, as he derives both prohibitions from one verse: “You shall not lie [tishkhav] with a man,” in the active form, as one can read the verb in this verse, written in the Torah without vowels, as though it stated: Enable your being lain with [tishakheiv], in the passive.

notes.he: דמפיק ליה מחד [קרא] אינו חייב אלא אחת:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Akiva: who derives it from one verse, he is liable only one.

messages.text: Evidently, Rabbi Akiva disagrees with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael with regard to a male who engages in intercourse with another male and a male who brings another male upon him to engage in intercourse.
Rather, the first clause is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, and with regard to one who blasphemes he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: אלמא לא סבר לה כר' ישמעאל אלא רישא וסיפא ר' ישמעאל ובמגדף סבר לה כר' עקיבא דלא בעי מעשה אע"ג דכתיב בעשותה ועשה אחת:
notes.en: Evidently he does not hold like Rabbi Yishmael. Rather, the first clause and the latter clause are Rabbi Yishmael, and with regard to the blasphemer he holds like Rabbi Akiva, who does not require an action, even though it is written “when [she] does” and “and does one.”

messages.text: If so, let the tanna also teach two additional cases with regard to bestiality: One who copulates with an animal, derived from the verse: “And you shall not lie with any beast” (Leviticus 18:23); and a man who brings an animal upon him for bestiality, derived from: “There shall not be a sodomite of the sons of Israel” (Deuteronomy 23:18), which can be interpreted as applying to all forms of male anal intercourse, including with animals.

notes.he: לר' ישמעאל דמיחייב ב' ליתני נמי והביא בהמה עליו וטפייה חדא:
notes.en: If so: according to Rabbi Yishmael, who holds him liable to two, let it also teach “and brought an animal upon himself,” and add one.

messages.text: With regard to one who copulates with an animal, and who brings an animal upon him to engage in bestiality, even according to the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael he is liable to bring only one sin offering, as when the verse: “There shall not be a sodomite,” is written, it is written with regard to men, i.e., the term sodomite does not include one who engages in bestiality.

notes.he: וכי כתיב לא יהיה קדש בגברי כתיב. דלא יהא נשכב לאדם ולא לבהמה. והאי דקא בעי הכא בזכר אזהרה לנשכב מה שאין כן בשאר עריות היינו טעמא דבשאר עריות סגיא לתרוייהו בחדא אזהרה שהרי הנשכב נהנה כשוכב הבא על הזכר הנשכב אינו נהנה:
notes.en: Didn’t Abaye say, etc.: this is the answer. And when “There shall not be a sodomite” is written, it is written with regard to men: that he should not be lain with by a person; [it does] not [speak of] an animal. And the reason why here, with a male, a warning is needed for the one lain with, which is not so with the other forbidden relations, is that with the other forbidden relations one warning suffices for both, since the one lain with derives pleasure like the one who lies; with one who has intercourse with a male, the one lain with does not derive pleasure.

messages.text: In conclusion, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, the mishna is listing prohibitions transgressed by men, and therefore one should remove from the tally the case of a woman who brings an animal upon her to engage in bestiality, and add the case of a man who brings another male upon him to engage in intercourse, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael.

The mishna is listing prohibitions transgressed by men and not women, but one should not remove from the tally the case of a woman who brings an animal upon her to engage in bestiality. The reason is that the tanna of the mishna teaches thirty-three prohibitions for which a man brings sin offerings, and he teaches another three instances of karet in order to complete the list of transgressions for which one is liable to be punished with karet. Those three do not meet the same criteria as the other thirty-three, and the case of a woman who brings an animal upon her to engage in bestiality is one of those three.

notes.he: בגברי חשיב ודקא קשיא לך דאשה נרבעת תנא ל"ג חטאות חשיב בחד גברא בהעלם אחד ותנא אשה נרבעת ופסח ומילה לסיומינהו לכריתות:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar said: he counts with regard to men. And as for your difficulty about the woman who is the object of bestiality: the tanna counted thirty-three sin offerings for one man in one lapse of awareness, and taught the woman with an animal, the Paschal offering and circumcision to complete the [list of] karet.

notes.he: לעולם בגברי קא חשיב ולא צריך לאפוקי אשה הנרבעת דתנא תנא ל"ג חטאות ותנא ג' כריתות דלית בהו חטאת לסיומינהו להשלים ל"ו כריתות וממאי דתנא כריתות בלא חטאות מדקתני סיפא פסח ומילה דלית בהו חטאת דהני מצות קום עשה נינהו:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rava [our Gemara reads: Rav]: Actually he counts men, and there is no need to remove the woman who is the object of bestiality, for the tanna taught thirty-three sin offerings and taught three cases of karet that carry no sin offering, to complete them, filling out the thirty-six cases of karet. And from where [do we know] he taught cases of karet without sin offerings? From the fact that the latter clause teaches the Paschal offering and circumcision, which carry no sin offering, since they are mitzvot of “arise and do.”

messages.text: What supports this interpretation? As the mishna teaches in the latter clause: And one is liable to receive karet for failure to fulfill the mitzva of bringing the Paschal offering and the mitzva of circumcision, which unlike the cases of prohibitions enumerated in the mishna, are positive mitzvot. Why does the tanna teach the cases of the Paschal offering and circumcision?

And if you say the mishna mentions these positive mitzvot to teach that one brings an offering for unwittingly failing to perform them, does one in fact bring an offering in such a case? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

The entire Torah is juxtaposed to idolatry, as it is written: “You shall have one law [torah] for him that does unwittingly. But the soul that does with a high hand, whether he be home-born or a stranger, he blasphemes the Lord; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people” (Numbers 15:29–30).

verse.he: הָאֶזְרָח בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה׃ וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂה ׀ בְּיָד רָמָה מִן־הָאֶזְרָח וּמִן־הַגֵּר אֶת־יְהֹוָה הוּא מְגַדֵּף וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּהּ׃
verse.en: For the citizen among the Israelites and for the stranger who resides among them—you shall have one ritual for anyone who acts in error. But whether citizen or stranger, the person who acts defiantly reviles GOD; that person shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.he: בעבודת כוכבים הכתוב מדבר:
notes.en: And the soul that does with a high hand: the verse is speaking of idol worship.

notes.he: משום דכי דבר ה' בזה היינו שבזה על דבור ראשון לא יהיה. ותנא נמי כרת בהאשה הנרבעת לסיומא דכיון דליתה בגברי לית בה חטאת:
notes.en: The entire Torah is juxtaposed to idol worship: because “he has despised the word of the Lord” [Numbers 15:31], that is, he despised the first utterance, “You shall have no [other gods].” And the tanna also taught karet for the woman who is the object of bestiality to complete [the list]: since it does not apply to men, it carries no sin offering.

messages.text: The phrase “But the soul that does with a high hand, whether he be home-born or a stranger, he blasphemes the Lord” is referring to one who engages in idol worship, and it is derived from here: Just as idol worship is a situation in which the Torah says to a person: Sit and refrain from action, and one who transgresses this prohibition unwittingly must bring a sin offering, so too, with regard to every transgression in which the Torah says that one must sit and refrain from action, one is liable to bring a sin offering for performing the act.

notes.dh: מה עבודת כוכבים שב ואל תעשה
notes.he: וחייבין על זדונו כרת ועל שגגתו חטאת כדכתיב לעיל מיניה עז בת שנתה לחטאת:
notes.en: Just as idol worship is “sit and do not act”: and one is liable to karet for its intentional violation and a sin offering for its unwitting violation, as it is written just before: “a she-goat in its first year for a sin offering” [Numbers 15:27].

notes.he: שזדונו כרת ושגגתו חטאת:
notes.en: So too every “sit and do not act”: whose intentional violation carries karet and whose unwitting violation carries a sin offering.

messages.text: Accordingly, one is not liable to bring an offering for the unwitting failure to perform a positive mitzva, such as bringing the Paschal offering or circumcision.

Rather, isn’t it correct to conclude from the mishna that the tanna of the mishna taught thirty-three prohibitions for which a man brings sin offerings, which apply to one who acts unwittingly, and he taught another three instances of karet in order to complete the list of transgressions for which one is liable to be punished with karet? These three instances are a woman who brings an animal upon her to engage in bestiality, one who fails to bring the Paschal offering, and one who fails to perform circumcision.
messages.quote: teaches thirty-three prohibitions for which a man brings sin offerings

notes.he: והנך אחריני דהוו לא תעשה ואיתנהו בגברי אית בהו כרת וחטאת:
notes.en: And those others, which are prohibitions and apply to men, carry karet and a sin offering.

notes.he: תימה א"כ ליחשוב נמי הביא זכור עליו והביא בהמה עליו:
notes.en: To complete the cases of karet: This is puzzling: if so, let it also count “brought a male upon himself” and “brought an animal upon himself.”

messages.text: Conclude from the mishna that this is the case.
§ The mishna’s list of prohibitions for whose unwitting violation one must bring a sin offering includes one who desecrates Shabbat.

The primary labors of Shabbat are forty-less-one, and one is liable to bring a sin offering for each primary labor he violates. That alone totals more than the thirty-six cases mentioned in the mishna.
messages.lead: The Sages express their surprise at this ruling and say:

notes.he: ליתני ע"ה כריתות:
notes.en: They are forty less one: [so] let it teach seventy-five cases of karet.

notes.he: קא חשיב ליה בכרת אחת. אמרי והא שבת יש בו ל"ט כריתות לאבות מלאכות שלו:
notes.en: One who desecrates Shabbat: he counts it as one karet. They say: but Shabbat has thirty-nine cases of karet, for its primary labors.

messages.text: The tanna taught a case where his action was unwitting with regard to Shabbat, i.e., he was unaware it was Shabbat, and his action was intentional with regard to the prohibited labors, in that he was aware that the acts he performed were labors that are prohibited on Shabbat. In that case, the halakha is that he is liable to bring only one sin offering, as he committed only a single error.

notes.he: דסבור שהיום חול:
notes.en: He taught unwitting with regard to Shabbat: that he thinks today is a weekday.

notes.he: שיודע שמלאכות הללו אסורות בשבת דא"נ עביד לכולהו אבות מלאכות אינו חייב אלא אחת דליכא אלא חדא שגגה ומתניתין בתר חיוב חטאת נקטינהו לכריתות:
notes.en: And intentional with regard to labors: that he knows these labors are forbidden on Shabbat. Even if he did all the primary labors he is liable only one, since there is only one error. And our mishna lists the cases of karet by the liability for a sin offering.

messages.text: The verse states: “Speak to the children of Israel, saying: A soul that sins in error, from all the commandments of God that may not be performed, and performs from one of them [me’aḥat mehena]” (Leviticus 4:2). The expression “me’aḥat mehena” is interpreted in several ways. One of them is: There is an instance of “them [hena],” i.e., many unwitting transgressions, which is like “one [aḥat],” a single unwitting transgression, in that one is liable to bring only one sin offering. How so? When one performed many labors where his action was unwitting with regard to Shabbat but his action was intentional with regard to the prohibited labors, he brings only one sin offering.

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר נֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תֶחֱטָא בִשְׁגָגָה מִכֹּל מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא תֵעָשֶׂינָה וְעָשָׂה מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה׃
verse.en:
Speak to the Israelite people thus:
When a person unwittingly incurs guilt in regard to any of GOD’s commandments about things not to be done, and does one of them—

notes.he: דכתיב ועשה מאחת מהנה וה"ל למיכתב אחת מהנה מאי מאחת משמע פעמים שחייב מעבירה אחת הנה כלומר כמה חטאות ומהנה מעבירות הרבה חטאת אחת:
notes.en: “Them” that is “one”: as it is written, “and performs from one of them [me’aḥat mehena]”; it could have written “one of them [aḥat mehena]”; what does “from one [me’aḥat]” mean? Sometimes from a single transgression one is liable “them,” that is, several sin offerings; and “from them [mehena]”: for many transgressions, one sin offering.

notes.he: ועשה מלאכות הרבה אינו חייב אלא אחת:
notes.en: Unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to labors: and he did many labors; he is liable only one.

messages.text: That is the case referred to in the mishna.

But let the tanna teach a case where his action was intentional with regard to Shabbat, i.e., he knew it was Shabbat, but his action was unwitting with regard to the prohibited labors, as he was unaware they were prohibited. In that case, the halakha is that he is liable to bring forty-less-one sin offerings, one for each primary category of labor.
messages.quote: unwitting with regard to Shabbat … intentional with regard to the prohibited labors

notes.he: דיודע שהיום שבת:
notes.en: Intentional with regard to Shabbat: that he knows today is Shabbat.

notes.he: דאינו יודע שמלאכות הללו אסורות אבל יודע מצות שבת בדבר אחד כגון דידע שאסור לצאת חוץ לתחום:
notes.en: And unwitting with regard to labors: that he does not know these labors are forbidden, but he knows the mitzva of Shabbat in one matter, for example, he knows it is forbidden to go out beyond the Shabbat limit.

notes.he: אמר ר' יוחנן תנא דידן קא חשיב למחלל שבת בחד כרת קא מיירי בשגגת שבת וזדון מלאכה כדתניא הנה שהיא אחת בשעשה מלאכות הרבה ואינו חייב אלא אחת היינו שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכה שאינו יודע שהוא שבת אבל יודע שמלאכות אלו אסורי' בשבת וכיון דעשאן בזדון בידיעה אין בהן קרבן אלא על שגגת שבת בלבד. ואמאי מוקים המחלל את השבת דבשגגת שבת וזדון מלאכה מיירי דאינו חייב אלא אחת וניתני בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכה דליחייבה ל"ט כו':
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: our tanna, who counts one who desecrates Shabbat as one karet, is speaking of unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to labor, as it is taught: “them” that is “one”: when he did many labors and is liable only one. That is unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to labor: he does not know it is Shabbat but knows these labors are forbidden on Shabbat; and since he did them intentionally, knowingly, there is no offering for them except for the error about Shabbat alone. And why does he explain “one who desecrates Shabbat” as speaking of unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to labor, where he is liable only one? Let it teach intentional with regard to Shabbat and unwitting with regard to labor, where he would be liable thirty-nine, etc.

messages.text: The verse states: “And performs from one of them.” This teaches that there are times when one is liable to bring one sin offering for all of his transgressions, and there are times when one is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every transgression.
messages.lead: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

messages.text: There is “one [aḥat],” i.e., the transgression of one prohibition, which is like “them [hena],” i.e., many unwitting transgressions, in that one is liable to bring multiple sin offerings. How so? When one performs many labors where his action was intentional with regard to Shabbat but his action was unwitting with regard to the prohibited labors, he brings multiple sin offerings.

notes.he: על מצוה אחת כגון שבת חייב כמה חטאות:
notes.en: “One” that is “them”: for one mitzva, such as Shabbat, he is liable several sin offerings.

messages.text: The tanna prefers to state the case of one who performed many labors where his action was unwitting with regard to Shabbat but it was intentional with regard to the prohibited labors, in order to emphasize that he is not exempt from bringing at least one sin offering, even though he performed the acts of labor intentionally.

notes.dh: שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות עדיפא ליה
notes.he:
למיתני לאשמעינן חדוש דאע"ג דהזיד במלאכות לא מפטר מחד חטאת:
לישנא אחרינא שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות עדיפא ליה דמילתא פסיקא ליה דמכי שגג אשבת לא מיפטר מיהא מחד חיובא חטאת דא"נ שגג אף במלאכות מחייב חדא אבל שגגת מלאכות דליחייב בכל חדא וחדא לא פסיקא ליה דזימנין דמיפטר מהך חיובא כגון שגג אף בשבת דהעלם זה וזה בידו ואמרינן במסכת שבת (דף ע:) דלא מחייב אלא חדא והכי מסתברא דבשגגת שבת קמיירי מדחשיב גבי עבודת כוכבים במתני' חדא ותו לא מכלל דבשגגת עבודת כוכבים וזדון עבודות קמיירי דאי בשגגת עבודה איכא ד' חטאות בד' עבודות זיבח וקיטור וניסך והשתחוה:
notes.en:
Unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to labors is preferable to him: to teach us a new point, that even though he acted intentionally with regard to the labors, he is not exempt from one sin offering.
Another version: unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to labors is preferable to him because it is a categorical ruling: once he erred about Shabbat he is not exempt from at least one sin offering, for even if he also erred about the labors he is liable one. But unwitting with regard to the labors, so that he is liable for each and every one, is not categorical, for sometimes he is exempt from that liability, for example where he also erred about Shabbat, so that he was unaware of both, and we say in tractate Shabbat (70b) that he is liable only one.
And it is reasonable that [the mishna] speaks of unwitting with regard to Shabbat, since for idol worship the mishna counts one and no more. By inference it speaks of unwitting with regard to idol worship and intentional with regard to the rites; for if it were unwitting with regard to the rites, there would be four sin offerings for the four rites: slaughtering, burning incense, pouring a libation and bowing.

notes.he: דמתניתא שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכה עדיפא ליה למיתני לאשמועינן רבותא דאף על גב דהזיד במלאכות מן חד חטאת מיהא לא מיפטר ט"א משום הכי עדיפא ליה דבין שגג בשבת מיפטר לאפוקי זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכה דאם הזיד נמי במלאכה פטור לגמרי מחטאת:
notes.en: The tanna of the mishna prefers to teach unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to labor, to teach us a greater point: that even though he acted intentionally with regard to the labors, he is not exempt from at least one sin offering. Another version: that is why he prefers it [a note in the printed text: it appears it should read: for even if he also erred about the labors, in any case he is not exempt from one, to exclude, etc.], for whether he erred about Shabbat … [the printed text is unclear here] … to exclude intentional with regard to Shabbat and unwitting with regard to labor, for if he also acted intentionally with regard to the labor he is entirely exempt from a sin offering.

messages.caption: What one knew decides how many sin offerings Shabbat costs: one for forgetting the day, one per primary labor for not knowing the labors, as the two baraitot on “from one of them” teach.

messages.text: And likewise, you find that the tanna of the mishna taught in this manner with regard to idol worship, as he teaches liability to bring one sin offering, despite the fact that the sinner may have performed four prohibited rites: Slaughtering, burning incense, pouring libations, and bowing. How so? This was a case where, as with Shabbat, his actions were unwitting with regard to idol worship, as he did not know he was worshipping an idol, but they were intentional with regard to the prohibited rites, i.e., he was aware these rites are prohibited.

notes.he: העובד עבודת כוכבים דקתני במתני' דלא מיחייבי אלא חדא משום דבשגגת עבודת כוכבים וזדון עבודות מיירי:
notes.en: And likewise you find with regard to one who worships an idol, whom the mishna teaches is liable only one: because it speaks of unwitting with regard to idol worship and intentional with regard to the rites.

messages.text: What are the circumstances of performing an act unwittingly with regard to idol worship? If we say it is referring to a case where he was standing in a house of idol worship and thought that it was a synagogue and bowed there, and it turned out that he bowed toward an idol, in this situation he commits no transgression: Since his heart was directed toward Heaven it is not even an unwitting transgression.

notes.he: דאי נמי בבית עבודת כוכבים השתחוה לשמים לאו איסורא עבד וליכא חטאת:
notes.en: His heart is toward Heaven: for even if he bowed to Heaven in a house of idol worship, he did nothing forbidden, and there is no sin offering.

notes.he: דהא סבור בית הכנסת הוא ולא מיחייב מידי:
notes.en: And his heart is toward Heaven: for he thinks it is a synagogue, and he is not liable for anything.

messages.text: Rather, one might say it is referring to a case where he saw a statue [andarta] in the image of the king and bowed to it.

Again, what are the circumstances of this case? If the baraita is referring to a situation where he bowed because he accepted that image upon himself as a god, he engaged in idol worship intentionally and therefore he is subject to death by stoning, and he is not required to bring a sin offering. And if he did not accept that image upon himself as a god and bowed merely in deference to the monarch, it is a meaningless act, not idol worship at all.

notes.dh: ה"ג אי דלא קבליה עליה באלוה לאו כלום הוא
notes.he: דכיון דלא נעשה לשם עבודת כוכבים השתחואה דידיה לאו כלום היא:
notes.en: This is the reading: “If he did not accept it upon himself as a god, it is nothing”: since it was not done for the sake of idol worship, his bowing is nothing.

notes.he: ואלא דחזא אנדרטא צלם שאינו עשוי לשם עבודת כוכבים וסגיד ליה מאי שוגג איכא הכא כיון שאינו עבודת כוכבים בהכי תליא מילתא אי דקבליה מזיד הוא ואי לא קבליה לאו מידי עביד ולא מיחייב:
notes.en: Rather, where he saw an andarta, a statue not made for the sake of idol worship, and bowed to it: what unwitting sin is there here, since it is not an idol? The matter depends on this: if he accepted it [as a god], he acted intentionally; and if he did not accept it, he did nothing and is not liable.

messages.text: Rather, it is referring to a case where one bowed out of love for someone who requested that he bow before the statue, or out of fear of someone demanding of him to do so. He was under the impression that unless he wholeheartedly has the intention to worship the idol there is no prohibition involved. This is an unwitting transgression.

notes.he: השתחוה לעבודת כוכבים מאהבת אדם ומיראת אדם דסבר מותר לעבוד עבודת כוכבים מאהבה ומיראה וזדון מלאכות קרי משמתכוין לעבוד:
notes.en: Rather: he bowed to an idol out of love for a person or fear of a person, for he thought it is permitted to worship an idol out of love and fear. And it is called intentional with regard to the rites, since he means to worship.

notes.he: אלא כגון דשגג בעבודת כוכבים דסבר מותר לעובדה [משום] שאינו עושה אלא מאהבה של שלטון או מיראה וזדון (מלאכות) [עבודות] הכא ליכא זדון (מלאכות) [עבודות] דהא לא עביד במזיד אלא להכי קרי זדון (מלאכות) [עבודות] דמתכוין לעבוד מאהבה:
notes.en: Rather, for example, where he erred about idol worship, thinking it is permitted to worship it because he does so only out of love of a ruler or out of fear. And intentional with regard to the rites [the printed text corrects “labors” to “rites” here]: there is no intentional sin with the rites here, since he did not act intentionally; rather it is called “intentional with regard to the rites” because he means to worship out of love.

messages.text: This works out well according to Abaye, who says: One who bows to an idol out of love or fear is liable to bring a sin offering. But according to Rava, who says: One who bows to an idol out of love or fear is exempt from bringing a sin offering, what can be said? What are the circumstances of an unwitting transgression with regard to idol worship?
messages.quote: out of love … or out of fear

notes.he: העובד מאהבה ומיראה ומתוקמ' מתני' בהכי דהיינו שגגת עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: This works out well according to Abaye, who says he is liable: one who worships out of love or fear; and the mishna is explained in this way, as unwitting with regard to idol worship.

messages.text: 3b

Rather, it is referring to a case where one says to himself that this is permitted. He is under the impression that idol worship is permitted, and his unwitting act was the result of ignorance, not forgetfulness.

notes.he: לעבוד עבודת כוכבים דהיינו שגגת עבודת כוכבים ושגגת עבודות:
notes.en: Rather, where he says it is permitted: to worship idols; that is, unwitting with regard to idol worship and unwitting with regard to the rites.

notes.he: ואלא שגגת עבודת כוכבים היכי דמי באומר מותר שאינו יודע שעבודת כוכבים אסור לעובדה וזדון עבודה היכי דמי הא לא ידע דאסיר כיון דאיתכוין לעבוד קרי להו זדון ודמי האי כהעלם זה וזה בידו בין היא עצמה בין עבודותיה:
notes.en: Rather, unwitting with regard to idol worship, what are the circumstances? Where he says it is permitted, not knowing that it is forbidden to worship idols. And intentional with regard to the rite, what are the circumstances, if he does not know it is forbidden? Since he intended to worship, they call it intentional. This is like [the case where] he was unaware of both this and that: of [idol worship] itself and of its rites.

messages.text: As, Rava raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman with regard to Shabbat only so it could be determined whether to deem one who is unaware of both the essence of Shabbat and the specific prohibited labors liable to bring one sin offering, or whether to deem him liable to bring two sin offerings. But as for the possibility to exempt him completely, he did not raise such a dilemma before him.

notes.dh: דעד כאן לא בעא מיניה רבא מר"נ
notes.he: העלם זה וזה בידו מהו בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין סב.):
notes.en: For Rava raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman only: what is [the halakha where] he was unaware of both this and that? In the chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 62a).

notes.he: ואמאי חייב חטאת דעד כאן לא בעא מיניה רבא מרב נחמן בפרק כלל גדול העלם זה וזה בידו דלא ידע דהוי שבת ולא ידע דמלאכות אסירן אלא אי לאיחיובי תרתי דאי אמרת בתר שגגת שבת אזלינן לא מיחייב אלא חדא ואי אמרת בתר שגגת מלאכה אזלינן ולא בתר שבת מיחייב אכל אב מלאכה ומלאכה:
notes.en: And why is he liable to a sin offering? [A note in the printed text: up to here belongs to 3a.] For Rava raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman, in the chapter Kelal Gadol, only where he was unaware of both this and that, not knowing that it was Shabbat and not knowing that the labors are forbidden, whether he is liable two: if you say we follow the error about Shabbat, he is liable only one; and if you say we follow the error about the labor and not about Shabbat, he is liable for each and every primary labor.

notes.dh: אבל למיפטר לגמרי לא בעי מיניה
notes.he: הכא נמי גבי עבודת כוכבים לא פטיר לגמרי ומיחייב חדא:
notes.en: But to exempt him completely, he did not ask him. Here too, with regard to idol worship, he is not completely exempt, and he is liable one.

messages.text: You find an act performed unwittingly with regard to idol worship in the case of a child who was taken captive among the gentiles and never taught about the Torah, as he knows that idol worship in general is prohibited, but with regard to these particular objects of idol worship that he is worshipping, he does not know that they are prohibited.

notes.dh: רב פפא אמר משכחת לה בתינוק שנשבה לבין העובדי כוכבים
notes.he: שגגת עבודת כוכבים וזדון עבודות כגון שחזר ושמע שאותה עבודת כוכבים שישנה שם אסורה בד' עבודות הללו והני עבודות הרוב ידעי דאסירן:
notes.en: Rav Pappa said: you find it in a child who was taken captive among the gentiles: unwitting with regard to idol worship and intentional with regard to the rites; for example, where he later heard that the idol that is there is forbidden with these four rites, and most people know these rites are forbidden.

notes.he: (אמר) רב פפא [אמר] היכי משכחת לה באומר מותר כגון תינוק שנשבה קטן לבין העובדי כוכבים וידע דאסיר עבודת כוכבים ולא ידע הי ניהו עבודות דאסירן:
notes.en: Rav Pappa said: how do you find “where he says it is permitted”? For example, a child who was taken captive as a minor among the gentiles, who knows that idol worship is forbidden but does not know which rites are forbidden.

messages.text: And if you wish, say instead: You may even say this ruling is stated with regard to an adult, i.e., one who was not captured by gentiles as a child, and it is speaking of a case where he erred with regard to this verse: “You shall not make with Me gods of silver and gods of gold, you shall not make for yourselves” (Exodus 20:20).

verse.he: לֹא תַעֲשׂוּן אִתִּי אֱלֹהֵי כֶסֶף וֵאלֹהֵי זָהָב לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ לָכֶם׃
verse.en: With Me, therefore, you shall not make any gods of silver, nor shall you make for yourselves any gods of gold.

messages.text: This person thinks that when bowing to an idol is prohibited it applies only to an object of idol worship fashioned of silver or gold; but with regard to objects fashioned of other substances, such as wood or stone, it is permitted. And that is a case of an action that is unwitting with regard to idol worship but intentional with regard to the prohibited rites.

notes.he: דסבור אין עבודת כוכבים של עץ:
notes.en: Unwitting with regard to idol worship: he thinks there is no [forbidden] idol of wood.

notes.he: ואי בעית תימא אפילו בגדול [ולא] נשבה נמי משכחת לה באומר מותר כגון דקא טעי בהדין קרא כו':
notes.en: And if you wish, say: you can find “where he says it is permitted” even with an adult who was [not] taken captive, for example, where he erred about this verse, etc.

messages.text: The tanna teaches the general category of Shabbat and the general category of idol worship, without mentioning the details of how many sin offerings one would be liable to bring for transgressing each prohibition.

notes.dh: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא משמיה דרב ביבי אמר
notes.he: לעולם זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות נמי קחשיב ודקאמרת ליחשיב טפי תנא לא מהדר אלא על מצות שחייבין עליהן כרת:
notes.en: Rav Aḥa son of Rav Ika said in the name of Rav Beivai: Actually, [the mishna] also counts intentional with regard to Shabbat and unwitting with regard to the labors. And as for what you said, “let it count more”: the tanna goes over only the mitzvot for which one is liable to karet.

notes.dh: שם שבת קתני שם עבודת כוכבים קתני
notes.he: ולעולם בכל חדא וחדא איכא טובא:
notes.en: He teaches the category of Shabbat, he teaches the category of idol worship: and in fact each one contains many.

notes.dh: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא אמר
notes.he: תנא דמתני' שם שבת ושם עבודת כוכבים סתם קתני כלומר דאי עביד בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכה מיחייב אכל חדא וחדא אי שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכה לא מיחייב אלא חדא:
notes.en: Rav Aḥa son of Rav Ika said: the tanna of the mishna teaches the category of Shabbat and the category of idol worship without specifying; that is to say, if he acted intentionally with regard to Shabbat and unwittingly with regard to labor he is liable for each and every one, and if unwittingly with regard to Shabbat and intentionally with regard to labor he is liable only one.

messages.text: From where can one infer this is the case?

From the fact that the mishna teaches: One who engages in intercourse with a woman and her daughter, or with a married woman. But there is the case of one’s daughter from the woman he raped, which the mishna does not teach. The case of a daughter from the woman one raped is included in the category of intercourse with a woman and her daughter, yet it is not taught explicitly. Evidently, it is included in the general category of intercourse with a woman and her daughter.

notes.he: אלא אתיא הנה הנה אתיא זמה זמה במסכת חגיגה בשילהי פ"ק (דף יא.):
notes.en: But there is his daughter from the woman he raped, which is not written: rather, it is derived from “hena” “hena” and from “zimma” “zimma,” in tractate Ḥagiga at the end of the first chapter (11a).

notes.he: דתנא שם איסור ושייר מדקתני הבא על אשה ובתה ושייר בתו מאנוסתו דלא תנא בהדייהו:
notes.en: From where [do we know] that the tanna taught the category of a prohibition and left cases out? From the fact that it teaches one who has intercourse with a woman and her daughter, and left out his daughter from the woman he raped, which he does not teach with them.

messages.text: The tanna of the mishna teaches those prohibitions that are written explicitly in the Torah; he does not teach those prohibitions that are not written explicitly but are derived from the verses. That is the reason he does not teach the case of intercourse with a daughter from the woman one raped; it is not because he is teaching only general categories.
messages.lead: The Sages say in response to this inference:

notes.he: אמרין מהא לא הוי ראיה דכתיבן בקרא קתני ולא שייר בתו מאנוסתו דלא כתיב בהדי' אלא מג"ש אתיא לא קתני:
notes.en: They say: there is no proof from this. He teaches those written in the verse, and he did not leave out his daughter from the woman he raped; since it is not written explicitly but is derived from a verbal analogy, he does not teach it.

messages.text: But there is the case of one’s wife’s daughter, and the daughter of her daughter, and the daughter of her son, which are written explicitly, and yet the tanna does not teach them. Rather, you must say that he teaches the general category of intercourse with a woman and her daughter, which includes those cases. So too, he teaches the general category of Shabbat and the general category of idol worship.

notes.dh: ל"א והא איכא בת אשתו בת בנה ובת בתה דכתיבן
notes.he: באורייתא וחייבי כריתות נינהו ושייר ולא קתני אלא שם אשה קתני והנך נמי בכללן הכא נמי כו':
notes.en: [The comment opens with the abbreviation ל״א, usually “another version.”] But there are his wife’s daughter, her son’s daughter and her daughter’s daughter, which are written in the Torah and are liable to karet, and he left them out and does not teach them; rather, he teaches the category of “a woman [and her daughter],” and these too are included in it. Here too, etc.

messages.text: Did Rav Beivai bar Abaye actually say this, that the tanna teaches the general category of Shabbat and teaches the general category of idol worship? But wasn’t it stated:
messages.lead: raises a contradiction between one statement of Rav Beivai bar Abaye and another statement of his:
messages.quote: category of Shabbat and the general category of idol worship

notes.he: דרב ביבי אדרב ביבי:
notes.en: Rav Aḥa raised a contradiction: between Rav Beivai and Rav Beivai.

notes.he: במס' זבחים בפ' השוחט (דף קז.):
notes.en: But wasn’t it stated: in tractate Zevaḥim, in the chapter HaShoḥet (107a).

messages.text: One who offers up the limbs of an offering slaughtered inside the Temple outside the Temple, i.e., he slaughtered the animal within the Sanctuary in accordance with halakha but sacrificed its limbs on an altar outside the Temple, he is liable to bring a sin offering if he did so unwittingly. Likewise, if he sacrifices limbs of an offering slaughtered outside the Temple outside the Temple, he is liable.

notes.he: שנשחטה בעזרה:
notes.en: Inner limbs: of an animal slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.

notes.he: בהמת קדשים שנשחטה בחוץ:
notes.en: Outer limbs: a consecrated animal slaughtered outside.

notes.he: במסכת זבחים המעלה אברי פנים שראוי להקטירן בעזרה והקטירן בחוץ ואברי חוץ אברי קדשים (שיצאו) [ששחטן] בחוץ ומעלן בחוץ או חולין מעלה בחוץ לשם קדשים חייב שתים. וקשיא ליה לרב ביבי:
notes.en: But wasn’t it stated: in tractate Zevaḥim: one who offers up inner limbs, which are fit to be burned in the courtyard, and burned them outside; and outer limbs: limbs of consecrated animals that he slaughtered outside and offers up outside; or he offers up non-sacred meat outside for the sake of consecrated offerings; [there are] two [liabilities]. And it was difficult for Rav Beivai:

messages.text: If so, consider that which we learned in the mishna: There are thirty-six cases in the Torah with regard to which one who performs the action intentionally is liable to receive karet. They are actually thirty-seven, as there is the case of one who offers up the limbs of an offering slaughtered inside the Temple outside the Temple, and one who offers up limbs of an offering slaughtered outside the Temple outside the Temple.
messages.lead: And Rav Beivai bar Abaye raised a difficulty:

notes.he: התם בזבחים א"כ דתרי גווני העלאה איכא ניתני בכריתות המעלה חוץ לעזרה אברי פנים והמעלה נמי אברי חוץ:
notes.en: And it was difficult for Rav Beivai: there, in Zevaḥim: if so, that there are two kinds of offering up, let it teach in Keritot: one who offers up inner limbs outside the courtyard, and also one who offers up outer limbs.

messages.text: If Rav Beivai bar Abaye maintains that the tanna of the mishna does not tally all the relevant prohibitions but states general categories, what is difficult to him? Let him answer that he teaches the category of offering up in the clause: One who slaughters offerings and who sacrifices them outside the Temple. The tanna would not then need to list these individual transgressions.

notes.he: התם א"כ דחייב שתים הוה להו ל"ז כריתות ליתני המעלה והמעלה תרין זימנין כלומר חד לאיברי פנים בחוץ וחד לאברי חוץ בחוץ. ואמאי קשיא ליה כיון דקסבר שם שבת קתני נישני לנפשיה הכא נמי שם העלאה קתני וה"ה לאיברי חוץ בחוץ:
notes.en: There: if so, that he is liable to two, there would be thirty-seven cases of karet; let it teach “one who offers up” and “one who offers up” twice, that is, once for inner limbs outside and once for outer limbs outside. And why was it difficult for him? Since he holds that [the tanna] teaches the category of Shabbat, let him answer for himself: here too he teaches the category of offering up, and the same applies to outer limbs outside.

messages.text: Are these cases comparable? In the cases of Shabbat and idol worship the tanna taught their details in their places [abeinekheihon], on Shabbat 73a and Sanhedrin 60b, respectively.

notes.he: חשבון חיובי' תנא במס' שבת (דף עג.) ודעבודת כוכבים במס' סנהדרין (דף ס:):
notes.en: Are Shabbat [and idol worship] comparable? The reckoning of the liabilities of Shabbat is taught in tractate Shabbat (73a), and that of idol worship in tractate Sanhedrin (60b).

notes.he: במקומותן:
notes.en: Benekheihon: in their places.

messages.text: Consequently, with regard to karet, where it is necessary to mention them as part of a list of prohibitions that are punishable by karet, Rav Beivai bar Abaye answers that the tanna teaches the category of Shabbat and teaches the category of idol worship, but he did not need to specify the details in this manner. By contrast, with regard to bringing up an offering, does the tanna teach them in their place, so that Rav Beivai bar Abaye can answer in this manner?

notes.he: הוא גררא בעלמא דחשיב להו למצות שחייבין עליהן כרת איכא לשנויי שם שבת שם עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: And with regard to karet, where it is needed: it is merely incidental that he counts them among the mitzvot for which one is liable to karet, so one can answer “the category of Shabbat, the category of idol worship.”

notes.he: לא אשכחן ביה נכא דליתני במשנה תרי גווני העלאה:
notes.en: But with regard to offering up: we do not find a place for it in which the mishna teaches the two kinds of offering up.

notes.dh: אמר לך רב ביבי מי דמי שבת וע"ז תנא יתהון בכונכיהון
notes.he: פירוש כל אחד שנה במסכתא (כל אחד שבת במסכתא) שלו כל מלאכותיו וכל דינו הילכך גבי כריתות הכא דאורייתא הוא כלומר דאגב גררא דצריך להן הזכירן משום הכי משני שם שבת קתני ולא רצה לטרוח לפרשן שכבר מפורשין במקומותן אבל הכא גבי המעלה מי תנא יתהון בכונכיהון כלומר כלום יש מסכתא ששמה מסכת העלאות שמפורשים שם דנישני הכין דשם העלאה קתני אלא כיון שאין להן מסכתא היה צריך לפרש כאן המעלה והמעלה אהכין קשיא ליה לרב ביבי:
notes.en: Rav Beivai would say to you: are they comparable? Shabbat and idol worship, he taught them bekhonkheihon, in their places; that is, each one he taught in its own tractate, all its labors and all its laws. Therefore with regard to karet here [the printed text reads de’oraita], that is, he mentioned them incidentally because he needed them, so he answers “he teaches the category of Shabbat,” and did not want to take the trouble to spell them out, since they are already spelled out in their places. But here, with offering up, did he teach them in their places? That is, is there a tractate called “tractate of offerings up” where they are spelled out, so that he could answer “he teaches the category of offering up”? Rather, since they have no tractate, he would have needed to spell out here “one who offers up” and “one who offers up”; that is what was difficult for Rav Beivai.

messages.text: § It was stated earlier that Rabbi Elazar says that Rabbi Oshaya says: Anywhere you find two different prohibitions but only one punishment of karet is stated for both of them you should divide the sin offering between them, i.e., if one transgressed both prohibitions unwittingly he is liable to bring a sin offering for each.
messages.quote: Anywhere you find two different prohibitions, and only one punishment of karet

messages.text: If there are two punishments of karet and only one prohibition written with regard to a certain act, what is the halakha? Is one liable to bring a separate sin offering for each act?
messages.lead: In a similar vein, Rabbi Yirmeya raised a dilemma before Rabbi Zeira:

notes.he: אם עשאן בהעלם אחת חייב אחת או ב' מי מיחלקן כריתות לחטאות כלאוין אי לא:
notes.en: Rabbi Yirmeya raised a dilemma, etc., what is [the halakha]? If he did them in one lapse of awareness, is he liable one or two? Do [separate] karet punishments divide the sin offerings as prohibitions do, or not?

notes.he: מי חלוקין שתי כריתות לחטאות כמו לאוין אי לא:
notes.en: Two karet punishments and one prohibition, what is [the halakha]? Do two karet punishments divide the sin offerings as prohibitions do, or not?
