messages.text: Are you saying this in reference to one who slaughters offerings outside the Temple and one who offered up the limbs of offerings outside the Temple? These do not match your description, as these are two separate prohibitions.

notes.he: שוחט ומעלה איכא ב' כריתות באחרי מות וחד לאו בראה אנכי השמר לך פן תעלה עולותיך בכל מקום [וכו' וכל מקום] שנאמר השמר פן ואל אינו אלא לא תעשה אבל בשחיטה ליכא לאו בהדיא דהאי דכתיב בפרשת (ויקרא י״ז:ז׳) ולא יזבחו עוד את זבחיהם וגו' מוקים ליה בזבחים בפרק השוחט והמעלה (זבחים דף קו.) בזובח בהמה למרקוליס:
notes.en: Slaughtering and offering up: there are two karet punishments in [the passage of] Aḥarei Mot, and one prohibition in Re’eh: “Take heed to yourself lest you offer up your burnt offerings in every place” [Deuteronomy 12:13], and wherever it says “take heed,” “lest” or “do not,” it is nothing but a prohibition. But for slaughtering there is no explicit prohibition, for the verse written in that passage (Leviticus 17:7), “And they shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices,” etc., is explained in Zevaḥim, in the chapter HaShoḥet VeHaMa’aleh (Zevaḥim 106a), as referring to one who sacrifices an animal to Markulis.

messages.text: If one considers the matter according to the one who derives the prohibition from a verbal analogy, it is as though both prohibitions are written explicitly. As it is stated here an expression of bringing: “Or who slaughters it outside the camp, and to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it” (Leviticus 17:3–4), and it is stated there an expression of bringing: “Who sacrifices a burnt offering or sacrifice, and to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it” (Leviticus 17:8–9).

verse.he: אִישׁ אִישׁ מִבֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁחַט שׁוֹר אוֹ־כֶשֶׂב אוֹ־עֵז בַּמַּחֲנֶה אוֹ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁחַט מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה׃ וְאֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לֹא הֱבִיאוֹ לְהַקְרִיב קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה לִפְנֵי מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב לָאִישׁ הַהוּא דָּם שָׁפָךְ וְנִכְרַת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא מִקֶּרֶב עַמּוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or sheep or goat in the camp, or does so outside the camp, and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to GOD, before GOD’s Tabernacle: bloodguilt shall be imputed to them; having shed blood, that person shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.he: התם בזבחים בשחיטה נאמר הבאה ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו ובהעלאה נאמר (ויקרא י״ז:ט׳) ואל פתח אהל מועד לא יביאנו מה להלן בהעלאה ענש והזהיר:
notes.en: A verbal analogy: there, in Zevaḥim: with slaughtering, “bringing” is stated: “and to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it”; and with offering up it is stated (Leviticus 17:9): “and to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he does not bring it.” Just as there, with offering up, [the Torah] both punished and warned [so too with slaughtering].

messages.text: Since there is a verbal analogy linking slaughtering an offering outside the Temple to sacrificing one outside the Temple, it follows that just as there, with regard to sacrificing, the Torah did not prescribe punishment unless it explicitly prohibited the act, as it is written: “Take heed to yourself, lest you sacrifice your burnt offerings in every place that you see” (Deuteronomy 12:13), so too here, with regard to slaughtering, the Torah did not prescribe punishment unless it explicitly prohibited the act as a separate prohibition.

verse.he: הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן־תַּעֲלֶה עֹלֹתֶיךָ בְּכׇל־מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּרְאֶה׃
verse.en: Take care not to sacrifice your burnt offerings in any place you like,

messages.text: If one considers the matter according to the one who derives the prohibition from a juxtaposition, it is also as though both prohibitions are written explicitly. The juxtaposition is that the verse states: “There you shall sacrifice your burnt offerings and there you shall do all that I command you” (Deuteronomy 12:14). Here the verse juxtaposes slaughtering, in the phrase: “And there you shall do,” to offering up.

verse.he: כִּי אִם־בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה בְּאַחַד שְׁבָטֶיךָ שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה עֹלֹתֶיךָ וְשָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּךָּ׃
verse.en: but only in the place that GOD will choose in one of your tribal territories. There you shall sacrifice your burnt offerings and there you shall observe all that I enjoin upon you.

notes.he: [ה"נ] שוחט:
notes.en: And there you shall do: [this] too [refers to] slaughtering.

messages.text: This teaches that just as there, with regard to offering up, the Torah did not prescribe punishment unless it explicitly prohibited the act, so too here, with regard to slaughtering, the Torah did not prescribe punishment unless it explicitly prohibited the act. Whether one derives the prohibition by verbal analogy or juxtaposition, it is considered as though the Torah explicitly wrote a prohibition with regard to slaughtering, and therefore this would not meet the criteria of Rabbi Yirmeya’s dilemma.

notes.he: מאי קא בעית שמא שוחט ומעלה בחוץ קאמרת דאית בהו שתי כריתות בשוחט כתיב כרת דכתיב ואל פתח אוהל מועד לא הביאו ובמעלה כתיב כרת דכתיב אשר יעלה עולה או זבח ואל פתח אוהל מועד לא יביאנו וגו' הני ב' לאוין נינהו אי למאן דאמר במס' זבחים הבאה הבאה הביאו יביאנו מה להלן בהעלאה לא ענש אלא א"כ הזהיר והיכן הזהיר דכתיב השמר לך פן תעלה עולותיך וכל מקום שנאמר השמר פן ואל זהו מצות לא תעשה אף בשחיטה נמי לא ענש אלא א"כ הזהיר ותרי לאוין נינהו ומשום הכי מחלקין ואי למאן דמייתי לה בהיקישא ללאו דאמר קרא שם תעלה עולותיך ושם תעשה היינו שחיטה מדכתיב בהדי הדדי ש"מ להיקישא דמקיש שחיטה להעלאה מה העלאה לא ענש אלא א"כ הזהיר כו' כדאמרן והיינו תרי לאוין נמי ופשיטא דמחלקי ואי אמרת הא כתיב לאו בשחיטה דכתיב ולא יזבחו עוד את זבחיהם ההוא בזובח בהמה למרקוליס מוקמינן לה:
notes.en: He said to him: What are you asking? Are you perhaps speaking of one who slaughters and offers up outside, which carry two karet punishments? With slaughtering karet is written: “and to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it” [Leviticus 17:4]; and with offering up karet is written: “who offers up a burnt offering or a sacrifice, and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,” etc. [Leviticus 17:8–9]. These are two prohibitions. [Either] according to the one in tractate Zevaḥim who says [it is derived from] “bringing,” “bringing”: “he did not bring it,” “he does not bring it”: just as there, with offering up, [the Torah] did not punish unless it warned (and where did it warn? As it is written: “Take heed to yourself lest you offer up your burnt offerings” [Deuteronomy 12:13], and wherever it says “take heed,” “lest” or “do not,” that is a prohibition), so too with slaughtering it did not punish unless it warned; so they are two prohibitions, and therefore they divide. Or according to the one who derives it by juxtaposition to a prohibition, as the verse states: “There you shall offer up your burnt offerings, and there you shall do” [Deuteronomy 12:14], which is slaughtering, since they are written together; conclude from it a juxtaposition that juxtaposes slaughtering to offering up: just as with offering up it did not punish unless it warned, etc., as we said, so these too are two prohibitions, and obviously they divide. And if you say a prohibition is written for slaughtering, “And they shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices” [Leviticus 17:7], we explain that as referring to one who sacrifices an animal to Markulis.

messages.text: Perhaps you are stating your dilemma with regard to two prohibitions punishable by the death penalty and only one prohibition is written with regard to them, and your dilemma is whether one brings two sin offerings if one transgressed both unwittingly, despite the fact that only one prohibition is written with regard to both acts. What is such a circumstance? This applies in the case of a necromancer, who raises up the spirit of the dead, and a sorcerer, who places a certain bone in his mouth for it to speak of its own accord (see Leviticus 20:6, 27).
messages.lead: Rabbi Zeira continues to address Rabbi Yirmeya:

notes.he: איכא ב' מיתות דכתיב (ויקרא כ׳:כ״ז) אוב או ידעוני מות יומת דאו מחלק אי זו שיעשה ימות ולאו אחד דכתיב לא ימצא בך וגו' ושואל אוב וידעוני ובני קרבן נינהו דכתיב בהו כרת (שם) והנפש אשר תפנה אל האובות וקמיבעי לך אי מיתות מחלקות לחטאות והעושן בהעלם אחד חייב שתים אי לא:
notes.en: A necromancer and a sorcerer: there are two death penalties, as it is written (Leviticus 20:27): “a necromancer or a sorcerer shall be put to death”; “or” divides: whichever one he does, he shall die. And there is one prohibition, as it is written: “There shall not be found among you,” etc., “or one who consults a necromancer or a sorcerer” [Deuteronomy 18:10–11]. And they are subject to an offering, since karet is written for them (ibid. [Leviticus 20:6]): “And the soul that turns to the necromancers.” And you are asking whether death penalties divide the sin offerings, so that one who did both in one lapse of awareness is liable to two, or not.

notes.he: יומתו גו' דמיהם בם אבל מדכתיב יומתו לשון רבים לא משמע חילוק דבעריות נמי כתיב ונכרתו לשון רבים ואפילו הכי איצטריך קרא לחלק:
notes.en: Perhaps two death penalties, etc.: “they shall be put to death … their blood shall be upon them” [Leviticus 20:27]. The fact that “they shall be put to death” is written in the plural does not imply a division, for with forbidden relations too “they shall be cut off” is written in the plural, and even so a verse was needed to divide.

messages.text: This should not be a dilemma, as this matter is a dispute between Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish. As the Sages taught a baraita, where they list those liable to be executed by stoning, in tractate Sanhedrin (53a):
messages.lead: Rabbi Zeira further said to Rabbi Yirmeya:

notes.dh: הא פלוגתא דר' יוחנן וריש לקיש
notes.he: באלו הן הנסקלין בד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף סה.) דשמעינן דתרווייהו דאין חייבין עליהן אלא אחת הואיל בלאו אחד נאמרו הלכך אין חילוק חטאות ביניהן להכי לא חשיב אלא חד מינייהו דכולהו כריתות דתנן במתני' למניינא דחטאות תננהו כדאמרי' בריש פירקין אם עשאן כולן בהעלם אחת חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: This is the dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish: in [the chapter] Elu Hen HaNiskalin, in Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 65a), where we learn that for the two of them one is liable only one [sin offering], since they were stated in one prohibition; therefore there is no division of sin offerings between them. That is why [the mishna] counts only one of them, for all the cases of karet in our mishna were taught for the count of sin offerings, as we said at the beginning of our chapter: if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness he is liable for each one.

messages.text: A necromancer and a sorcerer,

and the following presents a difficulty to us: And what is different with regard to stonings that the tanna teaches the case of a sorcerer, but the tanna does not teach the case of a sorcerer with regard to the list of transgressions punishable by karet, thereby indicating that one is liable to bring only a single sin offering for both transgressions?

notes.he: אלא דילמא ב' מיתות ולאו אחד מיבעיא לך אי מחלקן לך מיתות לחטאות ומאי היא אוב וידעוני דכתיב בהו ב' מיתות מות יומתו באבן ירגמו אותם ולאו אחד דכתיב לא ימצא בך וגו' ושואל אוב וידעוני א"ל אין א"ל ר' זירא הא פלוגתא דר' יוחנן וריש לקיש אי מיחלקי אי לא דתנן בסנהדרין בעל אוב וידעוני גבי סקילה וגבי כריתות לא תני ידעוני אבל אוב בלבד ומ"ש דלא תני ידעוני א"ר יוחנן הואיל ושניהם בלאו אחד דלא ימצא נאמרו כיון דאין בהן אלא לאו אחד אינן חולקין להכי תני חד:
notes.en: Rather, perhaps you are asking about two death penalties and one prohibition: whether death penalties divide the sin offerings. And what is that? A necromancer and a sorcerer, for whom two death penalties are written, “shall surely be put to death; they shall stone them with stones” [Leviticus 20:27], and one prohibition, as it is written: “There shall not be found among you,” etc., “or one who consults a necromancer or a sorcerer” [Deuteronomy 18:10–11]. He said to him: Yes. Rabbi Zeira said to him: This is the dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish whether they divide or not, for we learned in Sanhedrin, with regard to stoning, “a necromancer and a sorcerer,” but with regard to karet he does not teach the sorcerer, only the necromancer. What is different that he does not teach the sorcerer? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: since both were stated in one prohibition, “There shall not be found”; since they have only one prohibition they do not divide, and that is why he teaches one.

messages.text: The tanna in tractate Karetot does not count the case of the sorcerer on its own since both the sorcerer and the necromancer were stated in one prohibition: “Do not turn to the necromancers and the sorcerers” (Leviticus 19:31); therefore, there is no separate obligation to bring an offering for each of them.
messages.quote: does not teach the case of a sorcerer with regard to the list of transgressions punishable by karet

verse.he: אַל־תִּפְנוּ אֶל־הָאֹבֹת וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִים אַל־תְּבַקְשׁוּ לְטׇמְאָה בָהֶם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: Do not turn to ghosts and do not inquire of familiar spirits, to be defiled by them: I the ETERNAL am your God.

messages.text: And let the tanna say the case of a sorcerer and let him not say the case of a necromancer, rather than the reverse.

notes.he: וניתני ידעוני במתניתין ולא ניתני בעל אוב מאי שנא דתני בעל אוב:
notes.en: And let him teach the sorcerer in the mishna and not teach the necromancer; what is different that he teaches the necromancer?

messages.text: The tanna maintains that since the verse opened with the case of a necromancer, it is proper to list that transgression and omit the case of a sorcerer.

notes.he: קסבר הואיל ובו פתח הכתוב דבכל התורה מקדים בעל אוב לידעוני:
notes.en: He holds: since the verse opened with it, for throughout the Torah [the verse] puts the necromancer before the sorcerer.

messages.text: The case of the sorcerer is not included in the list of transgressions punishable by karet since it does not involve an action, but only speech, through the use of a bone, and one does not bring a sin offering for a prohibition that does not involve an action.
messages.quote: does not teach the case of a sorcerer

notes.he: הילכך לאו בר קרבן הוא אבל אוב יש בו מעשה שמנקש בזרועותיו ומדבר משחיו:
notes.en: Since it does not involve an action: therefore it is not subject to an offering. But the necromancer’s sin involves an action, for he knocks with his arms and speaks from his armpits.

notes.he: ידעוני מכניס עצם חיה ששמה ידוע לתוך פיו ומדבר:
notes.en: A sorcerer [yidde’oni] puts the bone of an animal called yadua into his mouth, and it speaks.

notes.he: תימה דלעיל אמר דתנא ג' כריתות לסיומינהו לכריתות אלמא אע"ג דלית בהו חיוב חטאת ה"נ ליתני ידעוני דכרת מיהא אית ביה:
notes.en: Since it does not involve an action: This is puzzling: above it said the tanna taught three cases of karet to complete the list of karet, so evidently [he taught them] even though they carry no liability for a sin offering. So too, let him teach the sorcerer, which at least carries karet.

notes.dh: וריש לקיש אמר הואיל ואין בו מעשה
notes.he: בידעוני אלא שמניח עצם ידוע בפיו והוא העצם מדבר מאליו בלא הקשת שפתיו הלכך לית ביה חילוק הא אי הוה ביה מעשה הוו חולקין אע"ג דלאו אחר:
notes.en: And Reish Lakish said: since it does not involve an action: the sorcerer, for he only puts the yadua bone in his mouth and the bone speaks by itself, without the twisting of his lips; therefore there is no division for it. But if there were an action in it, they would divide, even though [there is] one prohibition.

messages.text: And as for Reish Lakish, what is the reason he does not state an explanation in accordance with the explanation of Rabbi Yoḥanan?

notes.dh: ריש לקיש מ"ט לא אמר כר' יוחנן
notes.he: כדקאמר ושניהם בלאו אחד נאמרו ושוו בהדדי ולית בהו חילוק:
notes.en: Reish Lakish, what is the reason he does not say like Rabbi Yoḥanan, as he says, that both were stated in one prohibition, are equal to each other and have no division?

messages.text: Reish Lakish disagrees with the explanation of Rabbi Yoḥanan because the cases of a necromancer and a sorcerer are divided in the verse with regard to the issue of the death penalty, i.e., one is liable to receive the death penalty for transgressing either prohibition, as it is stated: “And a man also or a woman, who are a necromancer or a sorcerer shall be put to death” (Leviticus 20:27). Consequently, one would be liable to bring a separate sin offering for the unwitting transgression of either prohibition were it not for the fact that sorcery does not involve an action.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אוֹ־אִשָּׁה כִּי־יִהְיֶה בָהֶם אוֹב אוֹ יִדְּעֹנִי מוֹת יוּמָתוּ בָּאֶבֶן יִרְגְּמוּ אֹתָם דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם׃ {פ}
verse.en: A man or a woman who has a ghost or a familiar spirit shall be put to death; they shall be pelted with stones—and the bloodguilt is theirs.

notes.he: ואי לאו הטעם דלית ביה מעשה מיתות מחלקן לחטאות דהא חלוקין הן במיתות וה"ל למיתנינהו אי הוה בר קרבן:
notes.en: For they are divided with regard to death penalties: and were it not for the reason that it involves no action, the death penalties would divide the sin offerings, since they are divided in the death penalties; and [the tanna] would have taught them [both] had it been subject to an offering.

notes.he: קסבר ריש לקיש דהא חלוקין הן במיתות מות יומתו חלוקין הן לחטאות אי הוי מעשה בידעוני:
notes.en: Rav Pappa said: Reish Lakish holds that since they are divided in [their] death penalties, “shall surely be put to death,” they would be divided for sin offerings if the sorcerer’s sin involved an action.

messages.text: And Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you that a division of a prohibition is considered a division that leads to separate sin offerings, whereas a division of separate death penalties is not considered a division in this regard.

notes.he: אמר לך חלוקה דמיתה לא הויא חלוקה בקרבן דחטאת אמאי אתי על לאו. חלוקה דלאו אי הוו בהו תרי לאוין הויא חלוקה לקרבן השתא כיון דלית להו אלא לאו אחד ושני מיתות חלוקה דמיתה לא הויא חלוקה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan would say to you: a division of death is not a division for an offering, for what does a sin offering come for? For a prohibition. A division of prohibition, if they had two prohibitions, would be a division for an offering; now, since they have only one prohibition and two death penalties, a division of death is not a division.

notes.he: דמאחר שמת אינו חוזר ומת ולהכי תני לה לתרויהו דסד"א לא לימות עד דעביד תרוייהו קמ"ל דהי דעביד חייב סקילה:
notes.en: A division of death is not a division: for once he has died he does not die again. And this is why [the verse] states it for both of them: it might enter your mind that he is not put to death until he does both of them; it teaches us that whichever one he does, he is liable to stoning.

messages.caption: Rabbi Hoshaya’s rule and Rabbi Yirmeya’s dilemma side by side: the anointing oil, slaughtering and offering up outside, and the necromancer and the sorcerer.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Yoḥanan, what is the reason he does not state an explanation in accordance with the explanation of Reish Lakish, who says the prohibition with regard to a sorcerer is not counted because it does not involve an action?

notes.dh: ור' יוחנן מ"ט לא אמר כריש לקיש
notes.he: דמשום ההוא טעמא אין חלוקין דאין בהו מעשה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan, what is the reason he does not say like Reish Lakish, that they are not divided for that reason, because they involve no action?

messages.text: Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains: Who is the tanna who taught the list of those liable to receive karet? It is Rabbi Akiva, who says: An action is not required for one to be liable to bring a sin offering.

notes.he: לקמן (כריתות דף ד.) מגדף מביא קרבן דלא בעינן מעשה:
notes.en: It is Rabbi Akiva, who said: below (Keritot 4a) that the blasphemer brings an offering, for we do not require an action.

notes.he: ר' יוחנן מאן תנא מתני' דכריתות ר' עקיבא היא דאמר לא בעינן מעשה דאפי' כי לית ביה מעשה (לית ביה חילוק חטאת) כדסבירא (ד)ליה במגדף דחייב חטאת אע"ג דלית ביה מעשה כדתרצינן מתני' בשמעתין דלעיל הילכך טעמא דידי דלית בהו חילוק משום דשניהם בלאו אחד נאמר:
notes.en: He holds: Rabbi Yoḥanan [says]: who taught the mishna of Keritot? It is Rabbi Akiva, who says we do not require an action, for even when there is no action in it [a note in the printed text: it appears it should read: and even when there is no action in it, in any case there is liability for a sin offering, as he holds, etc.] (there is no division of sin offerings), as he holds with regard to the blasphemer, that he is liable to a sin offering even though there is no action in it, as we explained the mishna in the discussion above. Therefore my reason that they have no division is that both were stated in one prohibition.

messages.text: And as for Reish Lakish, how does he respond to this claim? He could say that although Rabbi Akiva does not require a significant action for one to be liable to bring a sin offering, nevertheless he does require a minor action. The transgression of a sorcerer involves no action, as the voice emerges of its own accord, and therefore even Rabbi Akiva would not hold one liable to bring a sin offering for the unwitting violation of this prohibition.

notes.he: מדקתני מגדף:
notes.en: Granted, he does not require a significant action: as is clear from the fact that it teaches the blasphemer.

notes.he: אמר לך אנא ודאי כרבנן סבירא לי דבעו מעשה אלא אפי' מתני' ר' עקיבא כדקאמרת אפי' הכי לא קשיא לי נהי דלא בעי ר' עקיבא מעשה רבה כרבנן מעשה זוטא מיהא בעי לאפוקי ידעוני דלית ביה אפי' מעשה זוטא כלל והלכך לא הוי חילוק ובעל אוב לר' עקיבא מאי מעשה זוטא אית ביה הקשת זרועותיו שמקיש זרועותיו זה בזה ומדבר מבין שחיו ומבין אצילי ידיו ע"י כישוף:
notes.en: And Reish Lakish would say to you: I certainly hold like the Rabbis, who require an action. But even if the mishna is Rabbi Akiva, as you say, it is still not difficult for me: granted that Rabbi Akiva does not require a significant action as the Rabbis do, he requires at least a minor action, which excludes the sorcerer, whose sin involves no action at all, not even a minor one; and therefore there is no division. And the necromancer, according to Rabbi Akiva, what minor action does his sin involve? The knocking of his arms: he knocks his arms against each other and speaks from between his armpits and from the joints of his arms, by sorcery.

messages.text: In the case of a necromancer, what action is there in this transgression? The striking of his arms against each other to raise the spirit of the dead is considered an action.

In the case of one who blasphemes, who merely speaks, what action is there in this transgression? Since Rabbi Akiva holds that an unwitting blasphemer is liable to bring a sin offering, this apparently indicates that no action at all is necessary. The twisting of his lips while he speaks is considered an action.

notes.he: ומגדף אית ביה מעשה זוטא עקימת שפתותיו:
notes.en: And the blasphemer’s sin involves a minor action: the twisting of his lips.

messages.text: It enters our mind that the striking of the necromancer’s arms against each other is considered a minor action even according to the opinion of the Rabbis, and they would deem him liable.

notes.he: מדקאמר ר"ל הקשת זרועותיו הוי מעשה וחזינן במתני' דפליגי רבנן אמגדף ולא פליגי אבעל אוב ש"מ דאפי' לרבנן חשיב מעשה:
notes.en: It entered our mind: since Reish Lakish said that knocking his arms is an action, and we see in the mishna that the Rabbis dispute about the blasphemer but do not dispute about the necromancer, conclude from it that even according to the Rabbis it counts as an action.

notes.he: דהקשת זרועותיו לריש לקיש הוי מעשה זוטא אפילו מדרבנן מדלא פליגי רבנן בבעל אוב כדפליגי במגדף:
notes.en: It entered our mind: that the knocking of his arms is, according to Reish Lakish, a minor action even according to the Rabbis, since the Rabbis do not dispute about the necromancer as they dispute about the blasphemer.

messages.text: With regard to idol worship, one is liable to be punished only for a matter that involves an action, for example where one slaughtered an offering, or burned incense, or poured a libation, or bowed.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:

messages.text: And the following matter poses a difficulty to us: Bowing does not involve an action.

In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, who says: An action is not required for one to be liable to bring a sin offering for transgressing a prohibition.
messages.quote: Bowing does not involve an action

messages.text: You may even say that the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, as the bending of his height when he bows is considered an action.

One can conclude from here by inference that Reish Lakish maintains that according to the opinion of the Rabbis, the bending of his height is not considered an action. If so, can it be said that the striking of his arms against each other, which is less of a movement than bending one’s height, is considered an action?

But rather, you must explain that when Reish Lakish says the striking of his arms against each other is considered a minor action, he is speaking only in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva; but according to the opinion of the Rabbis it is not considered an action.

If so, that the Rabbis hold that the necromancer does not perform an action, why does the mishna teach that the Rabbis say: The list in the mishna is excluding one who blasphemes, as he does not perform an action, but rather he sins with speech. Let it teach instead: The list in the mishna is excluding one who blasphemes and a necromancer.
The tanna teaches one of two examples that the Rabbis could have mentioned.

notes.he: מיתיבי וכו' ניתני לרבנן יצא מגדף ובעל אוב דלית בהו מעשה אין הכי נמי דאי בעי למיתני אלא חדא מן תרתי קתני יצא מגדף וה"ה לבעל אוב:
notes.en: They raise an objection, etc.: let it teach, for the Rabbis, “excluding the blasphemer and the necromancer,” whose sins involve no action. Yes, that is so; [he could have taught both] had he wished, but he teaches only one of the two, “excluding the blasphemer,” and the same applies to the necromancer.

messages.text: But if that is so, let the mishna teach the statement of the Rabbis with regard to a necromancer and let it not teach the statement of the Rabbis with regard to one who blasphemes.

notes.he: וליתני יצא בעל אוב ולא ליתני יצא מגדף:
notes.en: And let it teach “excluding the necromancer,” and not teach “excluding the blasphemer.”

messages.text: It was necessary for the tanna to mention one who blasphemes, as it might enter your mind to say: Since its punishment of karet is written in the place where the verse discusses an offering (see Numbers 15:28–30), one might say that in this case the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Akiva that one is liable to bring a sin offering despite the fact that no action is involved. To counter this, the mishna specifically mentions the exclusion of one who blasphemes to teach us that this is not the case.

notes.he: כרת דמגדף. מישתעי קרא בקרבן עבודת כוכבים בסדר שלח לך נפש כי תחטא בשגגה והקריבה עז בת שנתה וגו' ובההיא פרשתא כתיב והנפש אשר תעשה ביד רמה וגו' ונכרתה דמישתעי במגדף וקסד"א הואיל וכתיב במקום קרבן ליחייב קרבן אע"ג דלית ביה מעשה קמ"ל יצא מגדף:
notes.en: Its karet: the karet of the blasphemer. The verse speaks of the offering for idol worship in the portion Shelaḥ Lekha, “And if a soul sins unwittingly, he shall offer a she-goat in its first year,” etc. [Numbers 15:27], and in that same passage it is written, “But the soul that does with a high hand,” etc., “shall be cut off” [Numbers 15:30], which speaks of the blasphemer. It might enter your mind that, since it is written in the place of the offering, he should be liable to an offering even though it involves no action; [the mishna] teaches us: “excluding the blasphemer.”

notes.he: סד"א הואיל וכתיב כרת דידי' במקום קרבן דכתיב לעיל והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה אימא מודו ליה רבנן לר' עקיבא דמעשה זוטא הוי מעשה וליחייב קרבן קמ"ל דלא ולהכי תנא יצא מגדף:
notes.en: It was necessary [to teach] the blasphemer: it might enter your mind that since its karet is written in the place of an offering, as it is written above, “And it shall be, if it was done unwittingly, hidden from the eyes of the congregation” [Numbers 15:24], I would say the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Akiva that a minor action counts as an action and he is liable to an offering; it teaches us that this is not so, and that is why it teaches “excluding the blasphemer.”

messages.text: The reason the Rabbis did not state: Excluding one who blasphemes and a necromancer, is that the action of the necromancer that the mishna teaches is referring to one who burns incense to a demon in order to raise the dead, which is a full-fledged action.

notes.he: היינו טעמא דלא פליגי רבנן אבעל אוב דלאו בהקשת זרועותיו מיירי אלא מקטר לשר השדים:
notes.en: Ulla said: this is the reason the Rabbis do not dispute about the necromancer: [the mishna] is not speaking of the knocking of his arms but of one who burns incense to the prince of the demons.

notes.he: במתני' דחייב חטאת לדברי הכל במקטיר לשד שיטענו לדבר מבין שחיו דהקטרה היינו מעשה רבה:
notes.en: Ulla said: the necromancer that the mishna teaches is liable to a sin offering according to all is one who burns incense to a demon so that it will cause him to speak from between his armpits; and burning incense is a significant action.

messages.text: If so, i.e., if the necromancer burns incense to a demon, this is the same as an idol worshipper, which is already mentioned in the mishna.
messages.lead: Rava objects to this answer from Ulla:

notes.he: מקטיר לשד היינו ע"ז:
notes.en: If so: one who burns incense to a demon, that is idol worship.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to one who burns incense to a demon in order to gather it together with other demons, i.e., he does not burn incense to a demon by means of a rite but in a manner of sorcery, to bring the demons to one place to then make use of them.

notes.he: שיתחבר אליו ויסייענו בכשפיו ולא קיטר לו לשם אלוה:
notes.en: In order to join him: so that he will join him and help him in his sorcery; he did not burn incense to him as a god.

notes.he: במקטר לשד שלא לשום עבודה אלא על מנת לחברו שיבא אליו ויקבוץ לו שדים הרבה שיעש' רצונו:
notes.en: Rather: where he burns incense to a demon not as worship but in order to join it, so that it will come to him and gather for him many demons who will do his will.

messages.text: @Rava If so, this is the same as a ḥover ḥever, one who gathers together, which is stated in the Torah as a separate prohibition (Deuteronomy 18:11) and which is a prohibition that does not carry the punishment of karet.
messages.quote: burns incense to a demon in order to gather it

notes.he: ולא בכרת הוא ולא במיתה הוא אלא בלאו:
notes.en: That is a ḥover ḥever: and that carries neither karet nor death, only a prohibition.

notes.he: שמקבץ כיתות של חיות ושל נחשים ע"י כשוף דאינו אלא בלאו:
notes.en: If so, that is a ḥover ḥever: one who gathers groups of beasts and of snakes by sorcery, which carries only a prohibition.

messages.text: It is true that such an individual is also a ḥover ḥever, but the Torah stated: A ḥover ḥever such as this, who gathers demons together, is included in the category of a necromancer and therefore his punishment is death by stoning, and transgressing this prohibition also results in karet.

notes.he: שמקטר לשר השדים הוא:
notes.en: A ḥover ḥever such as this: one who burns incense to the prince of the demons.

notes.he: א"ל אע"ג דמקטיר לשד על מנת לחברו לשום אוב היינו חובר וחובר חבר בלאו גרידא הוא התורה אמרה חובר חבר כגון זה דבעל אוב בסקילה ובשוגג חטאת:
notes.en: He said to him: even though one who burns incense to a demon in order to join it, for the purpose of necromancy, is a ḥover, and a ḥover ḥever carries a mere prohibition, the Torah said: a ḥover ḥever such as this [is a necromancer], for the necromancer is [punished] with stoning, and if unwitting, [brings] a sin offering.

messages.text: But then the case of a ḥover ḥever, which is a prohibition that does not entail karet, what is it?
As it is taught in a baraita:

With regard to the verse: “And a ḥover ḥaver” (Deuteronomy 18:11), this is referring to both one who uses sorcery and thereby gathers large beasts into one place, and also to one who gathers small beasts into one place, and even to one who gathers into one place snakes and scorpions; all of these individuals are liable.

verse.he: וְחֹבֵר חָבֶר וְשֹׁאֵל אוֹב וְיִדְּעֹנִי וְדֹרֵשׁ אֶל־הַמֵּתִים׃
verse.en: one who casts spells, or one who consults ghosts or familiar spirits, or one who inquires of the dead.

notes.he: שמחבר חיות גדולות ומצמדן יחד:
notes.en: Both one who joins large ones: who joins large beasts and binds them together.

notes.he: לחיות קטנות לוחש ומחברן בכשפים יחד:
notes.en: And small ones: over small beasts he whispers and joins them together by sorcery.

notes.he: שמקבץ כיתות של חיות גדולות:
notes.en: Both one who joins large ones: who gathers groups of large beasts.

notes.he: שמקבץ חיות קטנות:
notes.en: And one who joins small ones: who gathers small beasts.

notes.he: ואפי' נחשים ועקרבים דחייב על לאו דלא ימצא:
notes.en: And even snakes and scorpions: for he is liable for the prohibition “There shall not be found [among you].”

messages.text: In the case of this one, who through sorcery wants to gather together a hornet and a scorpion, this is prohibited. But if they are pursuing him and he merely seeks to defend himself, it is permitted.

notes.he: דלא חשיבי אסור ללוחשן:
notes.en: Even a hornet and a scorpion: though they are insignificant, it is forbidden to whisper [charms] over them.

notes.he: תימה ה"ד אי דאיכא סכנה פשיטא דאין לך דבר שעומד בפני פקוח נפש ואי ליכא סכנה אמאי שריא:
notes.en: And if they are pursuing him, it is permitted: This is puzzling: what are the circumstances? If there is danger, it is obvious, for nothing stands in the way of saving a life; and if there is no danger, why is it permitted?

notes.he: אמר אביי אפי' חובר למיצמד זיבורא ועקרבא שידחקו זה את זה ויהרגו זה את זה אסור:
notes.en: Abaye said: even one who joins them in order to bind a hornet and a scorpion together, so that they press against each other and kill each other, is forbidden.

notes.he: שרוצין להזיקו ומשום הכי מחברן שלא יזיקוהו שרי:
notes.en: And if they are coming after him: that is, they want to harm him, and for that reason he joins them so that they will not harm him, it is permitted.

messages.text: According to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says the bending of one’s height is considered an action, the twisting of…

notes.he: הקשת שפתיו דמגדף לרבנן להוי מעשה ואמאי קא אמרי יצא מגדף:
notes.en: The twisting of the blasphemer’s lips should, according to the Rabbis, be an action; so why do they say “excluding the blasphemer”?

messages.text: Continued on 4a: …his lips should be considered an action in the case of one who blasphemes. Rava answers that the blasphemer is different, since his sin is primarily in the heart.
